docs.title: Any Texts Statistics (anyTS)
docs.text: anyTS is the language-independent core of the text statistics libraries ruTS (Russian) and esTS (Spanish). It holds the code that does not depend on a language, so that it is written, tested and documented once; a language library adds its tokenizer, lemmatizer, spaCy model and rules and re-exports the core under its own names.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Extraction

    Extract sentences, words and character N-grams with extractors whose tokenizer, lemmatizer and number pattern are hooks a language library overrides

    Extraction

  • Statistics interface

    Give the statistics of every class through one interface: a dictionary, nested or flat, a pandas frame, a printed table and the reading of a statistic by its scale

    Statistics interface

  • Basic statistics

    Count sentences, words, syllables, letters and punctuation marks by type, with the syllables of a language library

    Basic statistics

  • Readability

    Compute Flesch reading ease, Flesch-Kincaid, Coleman-Liau, ARI, SMOG, Gunning fog, LIX, RIX, Legibilidad µ, the consensus grade and the reading time, with the coefficients of a language library

    Readability metrics

  • Lexical diversity

    Compute Type-Token Ratio and its variants, MATTR, MSTTR, MTLD, MA-MTLD, MTLD-W, HD-D, the indices of Simpson and Yule, entropy, the laws of Zipf and Heaps, over the whole text or over windows with confidence intervals

    Lexical diversity metrics

  • Lexical sophistication

    Measure a text by a frequency dictionary in the manner of TAALES: coverage, mean frequency, range and dispersion, surprisal and perplexity, frequency bands and lexical density

    Lexical sophistication

  • Style

    Compute the SEO metrics (nausea, water, spam, naturalness by Zipf's law, keyword density) and the markers of the officialese, with the lists and the morphology of a language library

    Style metrics

  • Cohesion

    Measure the cohesion between sentences in the manner of Coh-Metrix - the overlap of nouns, arguments and content words, adjacent and over all pairs, Dice, with the next two sentences and between paragraphs in the manner of TAACO, givenness, the repetition of the tense and the aspect - and find the connectors of a dictionary with the context rules of a language, with the words and the features of a language library

    Cohesion statistics

  • Syntax

    Compute the statistics of the dependency tree - dependency distances, tree depth, valency, coordination chains, clauses, modifiers of a noun, prepositional chains, participial clauses, the passive, negations, split predicates, the words before the root, the order of the subjects and the objects, the similarity of adjacent sentences and the T-units and phrases of L2SCA - with the clauses and the constructions of a language library, on tree helpers that read the labels shared by Universal Dependencies and ClearNLP and the verb form of a predicate by its auxiliaries

    Syntactic statistics

  • Morphology

    Count the parts of speech and the features of Universal Dependencies by value or word by word, with the descriptions of the values, the markers and the analysis of a language library

    Morphological statistics

  • Phonetics

    Compute classes of the sounds, consonant clusters, hiatuses, entropy of the CV patterns, alliteration and assonance by the repetition index, open syllables, with the transcription and the syllables of a language library

    Phonetic statistics

  • Corpus measures

    Compare corpora by keywords against a corpus or a frequency dictionary, collocations, the dispersion of a word, stylometry (Burrows's Delta and its variants, Zeta, Kilgarriff's chi-square, the Mendenhall curve), the comparison of corpora feature by feature with effect sizes, a bootstrap by texts and the Holm correction, and a KWIC concordance

    Corpus measures

  • Visualization

    Plot Zipf's law, vocabulary growth, sentence lengths, literature fingerprinting, a word tree, corpus and stylometric measures, with the labels of the plots as a parameter, and highlight a text by the layers of a language library

    Visualization

  • Components

    Build components of spaCy pipelines that put the statistics into an extension of Doc

    Components

  • Datasets

    Download an archive with a checksum, extract it safely and filter the records

    Datasets

  • Exceptions

    Catch errors of one hierarchy whose classes are also built-in exceptions

    Exceptions

The reference of every function is a named section that the libraries include in their own documentation, so a formula is described in one place.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Requires Python 3.11 or newer.

pip install anyts

The dependencies are on the Installation page.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
CodeResult 
from anyts import DiversityStats, SentsExtractor, WordsExtractor

text = "The cat sat on the mat. The dog sat on the log! The cat and the dog slept."
SentsExtractor().extract(text)

ds = DiversityStats(WordsExtractor(lowercase=True).extract(text))
ds.ttr, round(ds.entropy, 3)

('The cat sat on the mat.', 'The dog sat on the log!', 'The cat and the dog slept.')
(0.5, 2.864)

A language library subclasses the extractors and overrides their hooks:

CodeResult 
class Words(WordsExtractor):
    def lemmatize(self, word):
        return {"sat": "sit", "slept": "sleep"}.get(word.lower(), word)


Words(lowercase=True, use_lexemes=True).extract("The cat sat. The dog slept.")

('the', 'cat', 'sit', 'the', 'dog', 'sleep')

The corpus measures take lists of words:

CodeResult 
from anyts.corpus import keyness

cats = WordsExtractor(lowercase=True).extract("The cat sat on the mat. The cat saw a bird. The cat slept.")
dogs = WordsExtractor(lowercase=True).extract("The dog sat on the log. The dog saw a cat. The dog barked.")
[(keyword.word, round(keyword.log_ratio, 2)) for keyword in keyness(cats, dogs, min_freq=2)]

[('cat', 1.58)]

docs.title: Components
docs.text:
StatsComponent(nlp, name)

The base of the components of spaCy that put the statistics of a text into an extension of Doc: a component registers the extension when added to a pipeline and puts the statistics of every document into doc._.<name>. Writing components in general is described in the documentation of spaCy.

A component of the lexical diversity of the words of a Doc:

CodeResult 
import spacy
from spacy.language import Language

from anyts import DiversityStats
from anyts.components import StatsComponent
from anyts.diversity_stats import check_params
from anyts.utils import iter_doc_words


class Diversity(DiversityStats):
    def __init__(self, doc, window_len=50):
        words = [word.lower() for _, _, word in iter_doc_words(doc)]
        super().__init__(words, window_len=window_len)


@Language.factory("demo_diversity")
class DiversityComponent(StatsComponent):
    stats_class = Diversity
    stats_params = ("window_len",)

    def __init__(self, nlp, name, window_len=50):
        check_params(window_len=window_len, messages=self.messages)
        self.window_len = window_len
        super().__init__(nlp, name)


nlp = spacy.blank("xx")
nlp.add_pipe("demo_diversity", name="diversity", config={"window_len": 3})
nlp("The cat and the dog")._.diversity.ttr
nlp("?!")._.diversity is None

0.8
True

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description nlp Language - Pipeline the component is added to name str - Name of the component in the pipeline and of the extension

docs.title: Names
docs.text:
The name of the pipe is the name of the extension: nlp.add_pipe(factory, name="basic") puts the statistics into doc._.basic. Without name both take the name of the factory. The extension follows the pipe when the pipeline renames it (nlp.rename_pipe). A name taken by an extension of another package raises ParameterError instead of replacing it: at add_pipe, or at the first document after rename_pipe, which renames the pipe before the component learns its name. A component taken from another pipeline (add_pipe(name, source=other)) is the same object in both, so under a new name it writes to that extension in the other pipeline too; a separate component comes from the factory, add_pipe(factory, name=...). The same component can be added twice under different names, with different parameters. A document with no words - an empty string, whitespace, punctuation alone - passes through a component untouched, its extension left at None.

Serialization

A component keeps an object of statistics in doc._.<name>, and spaCy cannot serialize it: Doc.to_bytes(), DocBin(store_user_data=True) and nlp.pipe(..., n_process>1) fail with these components in the pipeline. To save a document, leave the user data out (doc.to_bytes(exclude=["user_data"])) or keep doc._.<name>.get_stats() separately; for multiprocessing compute the statistics in the main process after nlp.pipe, without the components.

docs.title: Components of the classes of statistics
docs.text:
Each class of statistics of the core has a component that takes its parameters in the config of the pipe, checks them at add_pipe and passes them to the class; a language library subclasses it, sets its subclass of the statistics as stats_class and registers it under its prefix:

@Language.factory("<prefix>_phon")
class PhonStatsComponent(anyts.components.PhonStatsComponent):
    stats_class = PhonStats  # the subclass of the library

The class of the core is the default of stats_class. Where it cannot read a Doc - an abstract class (BasicStats, LexicalStats, PhonStats), ReadabilityStats without the basic_stats_class of a library, none at all (DiversityStatsComponent, the class of the core taking a list of words) - the component cannot be added until the library gives its class.

Component Class of statistics Parameters BasicStatsComponent BasicStats - ReadabilityStatsComponent ReadabilityStats preset, basic DiversityStatsComponent set by a library window_len, mtld_threshold, mtld_min_len, hdd_sample_size, log_base LexicalStatsComponent LexicalStats - StyleStatsComponent StyleStats stopwords, top_n, nausea_stopwords, cliches PhonStatsComponent PhonStats window_len SyntaxStatsComponent SyntaxStats - CohesionStatsComponent CohesionStats - MorphStatsComponent MorphStats -

docs.title: Basic statistics
docs.text:
BasicStatsComponent(nlp, name)

BasicStatsComponent puts the basic statistics of a document into its extension.

docs.title: Readability metrics
docs.text:
ReadabilityStatsComponent(nlp, name, preset=None, basic=None)

ReadabilityStatsComponent puts the readability metrics into the extension, computed from the document or, with basic, from the basic statistics another component put into it. A library sets basic_factory, the factory of its component of the basic statistics, which the error names when that extension holds none.

Parameter Type Default Description preset str None Preset of the coefficients, one of the presets of the class; the default of the class if None basic str None Extension of a component of the basic statistics to reuse instead of computing them again

With preset left at None the config of a saved pipeline holds no preset, and the pipeline takes the default of the class when it is loaded; a library that wants its default written into the config gives it in the signature of its subclass.

Raises:

  • ParameterError - a stats_class that is not concrete, a preset that is not a string or not one of the class, an extension not named by a string;
  • SourceTypeError - a class without basic_stats_class and no basic;
  • SourceError - a document whose extension basic holds no basic statistics of the class.

docs.title: Lexical sophistication statistics
docs.text:
LexicalStatsComponent(nlp, name)

LexicalStatsComponent puts the lexical sophistication statistics into the extension, with the frequency dictionary of its attribute freq_dict: None by default, for the dictionary of the class, and set by a library in the constructor of its component. A document gets the statistics when it has a word of iter_doc_words (with join_hyphens) other than a number of the method is_number, anyts.utils.is_number by default; a library gives the numbers its class leaves out, so a document of numbers alone passes untouched.

  • ParameterError - a top_n that is not an integer of at least one.

docs.title: Sentences after blank lines
docs.text:
start_sents_after_blank_lines(doc)

A component that starts a sentence at the first token after a blank line - a line break, optional whitespace and another line break - so that a heading, a list item or a paragraph without a final mark is a sentence of its own, as in the sentence extractor. It goes before the parser, senter or sentencizer, which keeps its starts and places the others. The whitespace before such a start stays with the sentence before it, and the marks that open a paragraph (a dash of a dialogue, ¡, «) stay with its first word. Alone, the component leaves the sentences within a paragraph unsplit and sets partial boundaries (has_sents), so the statistics take the sentences of such a document from its text. A parsed document, such as one passed through the pipeline again, passes untouched, since spaCy keeps its sentences. A language library registers the component under its prefix, Language.component("<prefix>_blank_lines", func=start_sents_after_blank_lines).

Parameter Type Default Description doc Doc - Doc object CodeResult 
import spacy
from spacy.language import Language

from anyts.components import start_sents_after_blank_lines

Language.component("demo_blank_lines", func=start_sents_after_blank_lines)
nlp = spacy.blank("xx")
nlp.add_pipe("demo_blank_lines")
nlp.add_pipe("sentencizer")
[sent.text.strip() for sent in nlp("What is new\n\nFaster import. Fewer bugs.").sents]

['What is new', 'Faster import.', 'Fewer bugs.']

docs.title: For library developers
docs.text:
Language hooks of a subclass

A language library subclasses StatsComponent for every class of its statistics and registers the subclass as a factory under its prefix, Language.factory("<prefix>_<statistics>"), so that the factories of several libraries live in one process; declared as entry points of spacy_factories, they load with spacy.load without importing the library. The subclass sets the class of its statistics and checks its parameters in its __init__ before calling the __init__ of the base, so a wrong parameter fails at add_pipe. The components of the classes of statistics of the core already carry their parameters and checks; a library sets its subclass of the statistics on them.

Hook Kind Description stats_class class attribute The class of statistics made of a document, None by default; a component with neither a concrete class nor its own compute raises ParameterError at add_pipe stats_params class attribute The attributes of the component passed to the class of statistics as keyword arguments, none by default; a name the component lacks raises ParameterError at add_pipe compute(doc) method The statistics of a document, stats_class(doc, **params) by default; overridden by a component that computes otherwise, such as one reusing the statistics of another component prepare(nlp) method Preparing the pipeline when the component is added, such as the rules of the tokenizer; nothing by default accepts(doc) method Whether a document gets the statistics; by default whether it has a word (has_words) messages class attribute The messages of the errors by key, MESSAGES by default from_extension(doc, name, stats_class, factory=None) method The statistics another component put into the document, for reuse instead of computing them again; an extension without statistics of the class raises SourceError, which names the factory to add. The other component must accept every document the reusing one does, since a document it passes leaves None

docs.title: Datasets
docs.text: The base of a dataset and the functions that download, verify and extract its archive and filter its records.

docs.title: Dataset
docs.text:
Dataset(name, meta=None)

An abstract dataset: a name, a dictionary of reference information meta and the methods a dataset implements - iteration over the records, check_data, get_texts, get_records and download(force=False). repr gives the name of the class and the name of the dataset, <repr_name>('<name>'), and the property info is the name under the key name_key followed by meta.

Parameter Type Default Description name str - Name of the dataset meta dict None Reference information about the dataset

docs.title: Fetching an archive
docs.text:
fetch_archive(url, filepath, checksum, missing, force=False, user_agent='anyTS')

Downloads the archive of a dataset; when it is just downloaded or missing says the extracted files are not all in place, verifies it and extracts the files. The SHA-256 checksum may be in upper or lower case; an archive that fails it is removed and downloaded again once. The files are extracted aside, next to the archive, and replace the directory of the dataset (or a link in its place) only once complete, the earlier directory removed only once they are in place: an interrupted extraction or a failed replacement leaves the earlier files intact, and concurrent calls do not share partial files. The name of the archive needs an extension, since the directory is named after the archive without it.

Parameter Type Default Description url str - Address of the archive filepath str / Path - Path to the archive; the files are extracted into its directory, under the name of the archive without its extensions checksum str - SHA-256 checksum of the archive missing bool - Whether the extracted files are missing force bool False Download the archive even if it is already there user_agent str USER_AGENT User-Agent header of the request, the name of the library

A name of the archive without an extension raises ParameterError before the download, an archive that cannot be downloaded or fails the checksum twice DownloadError, an archive that cannot be extracted or files that cannot replace the directory of the dataset DataFileError, and a path of the archive that is neither a string nor a Path SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Downloading a file
docs.text:
download_file(url, dirpath, filename=None, force=False, user_agent='anyTS')

Downloads a file into a directory and returns its path, or an empty string if the file is already there and force is off. The name of the file is the decoded last part of the path of the address; an address without one needs filename. The file is written under a temporary name and renamed once complete: a broken, interrupted or cut download (shorter than the announced length) leaves no partial file, and concurrent downloads do not share partial files. The server is waited for at most DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT (60) seconds.

Parameter Type Default Description url str - Address of the file dirpath str / Path - Directory for the downloaded file filename str None Name of the downloaded file; the last part of the address by default force bool False Download the file even if it is already there user_agent str USER_AGENT User-Agent header of the request, the name of the library

A directory that cannot be created, an address without a name of a file and no filename, a name that is not a plain name of a file, such as one with a drive or a separator, and a broken, interrupted or cut download raise DownloadError, and a directory that is neither a string nor a Path SourceTypeError.

A language library passes its own name as user_agent.

docs.title: Extracting an archive
docs.text:
extract_archive(archive_file, extract_dir=None)

Extracts a ZIP or TAR archive and returns the directory with the files. Paths leading outside the directory (absolute, with a drive or a network share, or with ..) and links are refused before anything is written, on any version of Python. The archive is extracted aside and put in place once complete: a single root directory takes the name of the archive without its extensions (corpus_v1.tar.xz - corpus_v1), replacing an earlier extraction; otherwise the files go into the directory, replacing those of the same names and keeping the others. A file in the place of a directory or the other way round, or in the place of the archive itself, is refused before anything is replaced.

Parameter Type Default Description archive_file str / Path - Path to the archive extract_dir str / Path None Directory for the extracted files; the directory of the archive by default

A refused path, link or file, a missing file, a file that is not an archive, a corrupted or empty archive, a directory that cannot be created and files that cannot be replaced raise DataFileError, and a path that is neither a string nor a Path SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Checksum of a file
docs.text:
sha256(path)

Computes the SHA-256 checksum of a file as a hexadecimal string in lower case; a missing file gives an empty string.

Parameter Type Default Description path str / Path - Path to the file

A path that is neither a string nor a Path raises SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Conversion into a path
docs.text:
to_path(path)

Converts a string or a Path into a Path, expanding a leading ~, alone or before a separator, into the home directory.

Parameter Type Default Description path str / Path - Path as a string or a Path

Any other value raises SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Filters of the records
docs.text:
check_limit(limit)

Checks the number of records to take: None or a non-negative integer.

Parameter Type Default Description limit int - Number of records; None - no limit

Any other value raises ParameterError.

length_filters(min_len, max_len)

Returns the predicates that keep the records whose field text is at least min_len and at most max_len characters long.

Parameter Type Default Description min_len int - Minimum length of the text in characters; None - no bound max_len int - Maximum length of the text in characters; None - no bound

A bound that is not an integer or is below one, or a minimum greater than the maximum, raises ParameterError.

substring_filter(field, value, fold=fold_diacritics)

Returns the predicate that keeps the records whose field holds the substring value. Both are folded by fold, so the differences of case and diacritics a language ignores do not count. The substring is plain text, not a regular expression; a field that is not a string does not match. A value that is not a string raises ParameterError, and a fold that cannot be called SourceTypeError.

Parameter Type Default Description field str - Name of the field of a record value str - Substring to look for fold Callable fold_diacritics Folding of a string before the comparison 
fold_diacritics(value)

Lower-cases a string (str.casefold), decomposes it (NFD) and drops the combining marks, so Galdós and galdos are the same. A letter that Unicode decomposes into a base letter and a mark is folded too (й gives и); a language where such a letter is a letter of its own passes another fold.

Parameter Type Default Description value str - String CodeResult 
from anyts.datasets import fold_diacritics, length_filters, substring_filter

records = [
    {"author": "Benito Pérez Galdós", "text": "A long text of the novel"},
    {"author": "Rubén Darío", "text": "A poem"},
]
filters = [substring_filter("author", "galdos"), *length_filters(10, None)]
[record["author"] for record in records if all(f(record) for f in filters)]
fold_diacritics("Pérez Galdós")

['Benito Pérez Galdós']
'perez galdos'

docs.title: For library developers
docs.text:
Language hooks of a subclass

The class attributes repr_name and name_key are the name of the class in repr and the key of the name in info; a subclass overrides them.

In the core repr_name is "Dataset" and name_key is "name".

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text:
All exceptions of the library inherit the base class AnyTSError and a built-in Python class, and can be caught by either.

Exception Built-in class When raised AnyTSError Exception Base class, never raised itself SourceTypeError TypeError An argument is of an unsupported type: the source or the text, a text where a list is expected, an extractor, basic statistics of another class, a path, a hook that is not callable (a tokenizer, a lemmatizer, a measure), or a tokenizer, a sentence splitter or the parse, analyze, syllabify, transcribe or find of a class that returns what the core cannot use SourceError ValueError The source has no words, sentences or texts to compute a statistic on, lacks an annotation the statistic needs, or holds values it cannot take: a negative or infinite frequency, a matrix of distances that is not one ParameterError ValueError A parameter is out of range or not a finite number, a name (of a measure, a variant, a preset, a layer, a norm) is unknown, the labels or the axes of a plot are set incorrectly, or a layer of the highlighting asks for an annotation the source lacks UnknownStatError ParameterError, KeyError An unknown statistic is requested by name DatasetNotFoundError OSError The spaCy model is not installed or a dataset is not downloaded; the message gives the command that fixes it DataFileError ValueError The archive of a dataset cannot be extracted or is unsafe, or a line of a dataset file cannot be read DownloadError RuntimeError A file cannot be downloaded, is cut short or fails the checksum verification, its name is not a plain name, or its directory cannot be created

The classes are available from anyts and from anyts.exceptions. A language library re-exports them under its own names as aliases, not subclasses, so its base class catches the errors of the core too.

CodeResult 
from anyts import AnyTSError, ParameterError, WordsExtractor

try:
    WordsExtractor(ngram_range=(2, 1))
except ParameterError as e:
    print(e)

try:
    WordsExtractor(tokenizer=42).extract("The cat sleeps.")
except AnyTSError as e:
    print(type(e).__name__)

The lower N-gram bound is greater than the upper
SourceTypeError

docs.title: Messages
docs.text:
The errors of the classes of statistics (Stats and its subclasses), of StatsComponent, of the extractors SentsExtractor, WordsExtractor and CharNgramsExtractor, of ConnectorMatcher and of HighlightedText take their messages from the class attribute messages, a mapping of a key to a message, anyts.constants.MESSAGES in English by default, a read-only mapping shared by every class; the messages with fields in braces are format strings. A language library sets the messages of its language on its subclasses, messages = MappingProxyType({**MESSAGES, **own}), and they cover every error such a class raises itself; source_type_error of anyts.utils gives the error of a source of a wrong type by them. The functions check_params, calc_windowed, calc_reading_time, split_windows and sentence_rhythm take the messages as the keyword messages.

The shared checks of anyts.utils (check_integer, check_number, check_bool, check_words, check_sequence), which these classes call too, and the other functions of the core keep their messages in English.

CodeResult 
from types import MappingProxyType

from anyts.constants import MESSAGES
from anyts.diversity_stats import DiversityStats


class Diversity(DiversityStats):
    messages = MappingProxyType({**MESSAGES, "no_words": "Il testo non contiene parole"})


try:
    Diversity([])
except ValueError as e:
    print(e)

Il testo non contiene parole

docs.title: Collocations
docs.text:
collocations(words, window=5, measure='logdice', min_freq=2, node=None, top_n=None)

Collocation extraction - pairs of words that occur together more often than independence would give: fixed expressions, terminology, the combinatorics of a word. The measures of association are those of Sketch Engine and of nltk.metrics.association.

Pairs are ordered, as in NLTK: the right word occurs at most window words after the left one, each pair of positions counted once; window=1 gives bigrams. The measures take the pair frequency divided by the window (Church and Hanks 1990, as in NLTK), which keeps the expected frequency independent of the window and Dice and the minimum sensitivity at most one; freq_pair stays undivided. So with window > 1 an always adjacent pair gets a logDice of \(14 - \log_2 window\) (13 at a window of 2), not 14 as in Sketch Engine with its raw co-occurrence; 14 needs a pair at every distance within the window. node keeps the pairs with the given word on either side.

Words are compared as they are: case, lemmatization and stop words belong to the word extractor; lemmas suit fixed expressions, word forms suit grammatical constructions.

CodeResult 
from anyts import WordsExtractor
from anyts.corpus import collocations

words = WordsExtractor(lowercase=True).extract(
    "The cat was at the window and watched the birds. The birds flew away and the cat "
    "fell asleep at the window. Tomorrow the cat will be at the window and watch the birds."
)

collocations(words, window=2, top_n=1)
[
    (c.left, c.right, round(c.score, 2))
    for c in collocations(words, window=1, node="cat", min_freq=1, measure="mi")[:2]
]

[Collocation(left='at', right='window', freq_left=3, freq_right=3, freq_pair=3, score=13.0)]
[('cat', 'fell', 3.5), ('cat', 'was', 3.5)]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of the text in order window int 5 Greatest distance between the words of a pair measure str 'logdice' Measure of anyts.constants.COLLOCATION_MEASURES min_freq int 2 Minimum frequency of a pair node str None Word whose combinatorics is needed; None - every pair top_n int None Number of collocations; None - all of them

Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, and no words SourceError. An unknown measure, a window or a top_n that is not an integer of at least one, a min_freq that is not an integer and a node that is not a string raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
Collocation(left, right, freq_left, freq_right, freq_pair, score)

A list of Collocation named tuples by descending measure and frequency of the pair (ties broken alphabetically); pd.DataFrame(found) gives a table.

Field Type Description left str Left word right str Right word, occurring within the window after the left one freq_left int Frequency of the left word freq_right int Frequency of the right word freq_pair int Frequency of the co-occurrence score float Value of the chosen measure

docs.title: Measures
docs.text:
The measures of measure by key, with their names and descriptions in anyts.constants.COLLOCATION_MEASURES:

Key Measures Range Higher means mi Frequency of the pair against the expected one, in bits Any number A stronger association mi3 MI with the frequency of the pair cubed Any number A stronger association t_score Difference of the observed and the expected frequency of the pair Any number A surer association dice Share of the pair in the occurrences of the two words 0-1 A stronger association logdice Dice coefficient on a logarithmic scale 14 and below A stronger association log_likelihood Significance of the association 0 and above, nan when a word fills the text or a cell is negative A more significant departure from independence, for attracted and avoided pairs alike npmi MI normalized by the information of the pair −1 to 1 A stronger association min_sensitivity Smaller share of the pair in the occurrences of either word 0-1 A stronger association

Every measure is a function of the module anyts.corpus.collocations of the frequencies of the words and of the pair and the number of words:

Parameter Type Default Description freq_a int - Frequency \(f_a\) of the first word freq_b int - Frequency \(f_b\) of the second word freq_ab float - Frequency \(f_{ab}\) of the pair n int - Number of words \(N\) of the text

A pair of zero frequency gives nan for MI, MI³, the t-score, logDice and NPMI.

docs.title: Mutual information
docs.text:
mi · Church and Hanks (1990)

calc_mi(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

The pointwise mutual information of the two words; it overrates rare pairs.

\[ \log_2 \frac{f_{ab} N}{f_a f_b} \]

docs.title: MI³
docs.text:
mi3 · Oakes (1998)

calc_mi3(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

The mutual information with the frequency of the pair cubed, which favours frequent pairs.

\[ \log_2 \frac{f_{ab}^3 N}{f_a f_b} \]

docs.title: t-score
docs.text:
t_score · Church et al. (1991)

calc_t_score(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

The difference of the observed and the expected frequency of the pair over the root of the observed one; it favours frequent pairs.

\[ \frac{f_{ab} - f_a f_b / N}{\sqrt{f_{ab}}} \]

docs.title: Dice coefficient
docs.text:
dice

calc_dice(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

The share of the pair in the occurrences of the two words; it does not depend on the size of the text.

\[ \frac{2 f_{ab}}{f_a + f_b} \]

docs.title: logDice
docs.text:
logdice · Rychlý (2008)

calc_logdice(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

The Dice coefficient on a binary logarithmic scale, the default measure, as in Sketch Engine. It does not depend on the size of the text; below zero the link is weak.

\[ 14 + \log_2 \frac{2 f_{ab}}{f_a + f_b} \]

docs.title: Log-likelihood
docs.text:
log_likelihood · Dunning (1993)

calc_log_likelihood(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

\(G^2\) over the 2×2 contingency table of the two words: the observed frequencies \(O\) - \(f_{ab}\), \(f_a - f_{ab}\), \(f_b - f_{ab}\) and \(N - f_a - f_b + f_{ab}\) - against the expected ones \(E\) under independence. A word that fills the whole text, or a negative cell, as of a word paired with itself in a window above one, gives nan.

\[ G^2 = 2 \sum O \ln \frac{O}{E} \]

docs.title: NPMI
docs.text:
npmi · Bouma (2009)

calc_npmi(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

The mutual information normalized by the information of the pair: one means the words occur only together. A pair as frequent as the text is long gives nan.

\[ \frac{MI}{-\log_2 (f_{ab} / N)} \]

docs.title: Minimum sensitivity
docs.text:
min_sensitivity · Pedersen (1998)

calc_min_sensitivity(freq_a, freq_b, freq_ab, n)

The smaller of the shares of the pair in the occurrences of each word.

\[ \min\left(\frac{f_{ab}}{f_a}, \frac{f_{ab}}{f_b}\right) \]

docs.title: Corpus comparison
docs.text:
compare_features(table_a, table_b, labels=('A', 'B'), n_bootstrap=1000, seed=0)

Compares two corpora feature by feature. Each corpus is a table of the features of its windows, parts of the texts of about equal size, so the features do not depend on text length. The result has one row per column, by descending absolute Cliff's delta, the features without statistics last. The bootstrap resamples whole texts by the index level text; without it every row is a text of its own. A column missing from one table gives nan.

CodeResult 
import pandas as pd

from anyts.corpus import compare_features

short = pd.DataFrame({"length": [14.0, 15.0, 13.0, 16.0]})
long = pd.DataFrame({"length": [33.0, 35.0, 31.0, 29.0]})
result = compare_features(short, long, labels=("short", "long"), n_bootstrap=200)
result.loc[
    "length", ["mean_short", "mean_long", "median_diff", "ci_low", "ci_high", "cliff_delta"]
].tolist()

[14.5, 32.0, -17.5, -20.5, -14.5, -1.0]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description table_a DataFrame - Features of the windows of the first corpus, one row per window table_b DataFrame - Features of the windows of the second corpus labels tuple[str, str] ('A', 'B') Names of the corpora for the columns, two strings that give distinct columns n_bootstrap int 1000 Number of bootstrap samples seed int / Generator 0 Seed of the random number generator, a non-negative integer, or a numpy Generator; None - a random one

A table that is not a DataFrame, repeats the name of a column or has a column that is not numeric raises SourceTypeError; the other parameters are checked by check_comparison_params.

check_comparison_params(labels=('A', 'B'), n_bootstrap=1000, seed=0)

Checks the parameters of compare_features before the texts are processed: it raises ParameterError unless the labels are two strings that give distinct columns (("diff", "B") would repeat median_diff), the number of bootstrap samples is an integer of at least one and the seed is None, a non-negative integer or a numpy Generator.

docs.title: Statistics
docs.text:
For a feature with the values \(x_1 \dots x_{n_A}\) in corpus A and \(y_1 \dots y_{n_B}\) in corpus B (undefined and infinite values dropped; with fewer than two values on a side - nan):

Column Description mean_A, mean_B, median_A, median_B means and medians median_diff, ci_low, ci_high the difference of the medians and its 95% percentile bootstrap interval: both sets are resampled n_bootstrap times (bootstrap_median_diff) cohen_d \(d = (\bar{x} - \bar{y}) / s\), \(s\) - the pooled standard deviation; 0.2 - a small effect, 0.5 - medium, 0.8 - large (calc_cohen_d) cliff_delta \(\delta = P(x > y) - P(x < y)\) from −1 to 1; \(\lvert\delta\rvert\) < 0.147 - a negligible effect, < 0.33 - small, < 0.474 - medium, large otherwise (Romano et al. 2006; calc_cliff_delta) auc the feature as a classifier: the share of the pairs of windows with the value in A greater than in B, ties counted as half; \(\delta = 2 \cdot AUC - 1\), 0.5 - the feature does not tell the corpora apart u, p_value the Mann-Whitney U statistic and the two-sided p-value (scipy.stats.mannwhitneyu) p_holm the p-value with Holm's correction for the number of features (holm_correction) n_A, n_B number of windows with a defined value n_texts_A, n_texts_B number of texts behind those windows

The columns are anyts.corpus.COMPARISON_COLUMNS with the suffixes a and b replaced by the labels of the corpora. Cliff's delta and the AUC come from the same U statistic and agree; Cohen's d is sensitive to outliers and non-normality, so it is best read next to the delta.

Windows of one text are not independent

The test and the effect sizes take the windows for independent observations, which the windows of one text are not: with few texts the p-values are too small and reflect the chosen texts as much as the corpora. The bootstrap resamples whole texts (a cluster bootstrap), so its interval covers the spread between texts; it needs at least two texts on each side and is rough with few.

docs.title: Functions of the statistics
docs.text:
compare_values(values_a, values_b, n_bootstrap=1000, rng=None, texts_a=None, texts_b=None)

Compares two sets of values of one feature and returns one row in the order of anyts.corpus.COMPARISON_COLUMNS, p_holm left nan. Undefined and infinite values, missing ones (None, NA) included, are dropped with their texts.

Parameter Type Default Description values_a list[float] - Values in the first corpus values_b list[float] - Values in the second corpus n_bootstrap int 1000 Number of bootstrap samples rng Generator None Random number generator of numpy; None - a new one without a seed texts_a list None Texts of the values in the first corpus for the bootstrap; None - every value a text of its own texts_b list None Texts of the values in the second corpus

A value that is neither a number nor a missing one, values that are not a flat list and texts that are not labels of one type raise SourceTypeError; an n_bootstrap that is not an integer of at least one, texts not as many as the values and an rng that is not a numpy Generator raise ParameterError.

calc_cohen_d(values_a, values_b)

Cohen's d with the pooled sample variances (ddof=1); nan with fewer than two values on a side or without spread.

Parameter Type Default Description values_a list[float] - Values in the first corpus values_b list[float] - Values in the second corpus

A value that is neither a number nor a missing one (None, NA) and values that are not a flat list raise SourceTypeError.

calc_cliff_delta(values_a, values_b)

Cliff's delta, the share of the pairs where the first value is greater minus the share where it is smaller; nan for an empty set or an undefined value. Computed by sorting, in \(O((n_A + n_B) \log n_B)\) time and linear memory.

Parameter Type Default Description values_a list[float] - Values in the first corpus values_b list[float] - Values in the second corpus

A value that is neither a number nor a missing one (None, NA) and values that are not a flat list raise SourceTypeError.

bootstrap_median_diff(values_a, values_b, n_bootstrap=1000, rng=None, confidence=0.95, texts_a=None, texts_b=None)

The percentile bootstrap interval of the difference of the medians. With texts_a and texts_b whole texts are resampled, the median of a draw taken over the values of its texts; with fewer than two texts on a side the interval is nan.

Parameter Type Default Description values_a list[float] - Values in the first corpus values_b list[float] - Values in the second corpus n_bootstrap int 1000 Number of bootstrap samples rng Generator None Random number generator of numpy; None - a new one without a seed confidence float 0.95 Confidence level texts_a list None Texts of the values in the first corpus; None - every value is resampled on its own texts_b list None Texts of the values in the second corpus

A value that is neither a number nor a missing one, values that are not a flat list and texts that are not labels of one type raise SourceTypeError; an n_bootstrap that is not an integer of at least one, a confidence that is not a number in (0, 1), texts not as many as the values and an rng that is not a numpy Generator raise ParameterError.

holm_correction(p_values)

Holm's correction for multiple comparisons: the p-values are sorted in ascending order, the i-th is multiplied by (m − i + 1), where m is the number of defined values, then the running maximum is taken and capped at one; nan stays nan.

Parameter Type Default Description p_values list[float] - p-values

A p-value that is neither a number nor a missing one and p-values that are not a flat list raise SourceTypeError, and a p-value outside [0, 1] ParameterError.

CodeResult 
from anyts.corpus import calc_cliff_delta, calc_cohen_d, holm_correction

round(calc_cohen_d([2, 4, 6, 8], [1, 3, 5, 7]), 3)
calc_cliff_delta([2, 4, 6, 8], [1, 3, 5, 7])
holm_correction([0.01, 0.04, 0.03]).round(3).tolist()

0.387
0.25
[0.03, 0.06, 0.06]

docs.title: Windows of a text
docs.text:
split_windows(text, window=1000, min_words=None, *, tokenize=None, opening_marks=OPENING_MARKS, symmetric_marks=SYMMETRIC_MARKS, closing_marks=CLOSING_MARKS, messages=MESSAGES)

Cuts a text into consecutive windows of exactly window words, so the features that depend on length are comparable between texts. The rest is a window only with at least min_words words (by default a whole window, so it is dropped). A boundary goes before the first word of a window and its opening marks; symmetric marks, such as a straight quote or the dash of an aside, close the previous window when glued to its last word, or after a closing mark when whitespace follows them; a dash glued to the next word opens a line of dialogue, and a run of such marks goes as a whole. Windows are stripped of whitespace; window=None gives the whole text. The words and their positions come from tokenize, by default the words of WordsExtractor.

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text string window int 1000 Size of a window in words; None - the whole text min_words int None Smallest number of words in a window; None - a whole window, or one word without a window tokenize Callable None Words of a text with their start and end positions opening_marks Collection[str] OPENING_MARKS Marks that open a phrase symmetric_marks Collection[str] SYMMETRIC_MARKS Opening marks that close a phrase as well closing_marks Collection[str] CLOSING_MARKS Marks that close a phrase messages dict[str, str] MESSAGES Messages of the errors by key

A text that is not a string, a tokenizer that is not callable or does not give the words in order as triples of integer bounds within the text and a string, and marks that are not a collection of strings raise SourceTypeError, a window or min_words that is not an integer of at least one, min_words above the window and a mark of more than one character ParameterError. A text without words or shorter than min_words gives an empty list.

The marks of the core are those of anyts.constants: quotes, brackets and dashes open a phrase, the straight quotes and the dashes are symmetric, and the final marks, the comma, the semicolon, the closing brackets, guillemet and quotes close one.

CodeResult 
from anyts.corpus import split_windows

split_windows("One two three four five", 2, min_words=1)
split_windows('He said: "Go home." Then he left the room', 4)

['One two', 'three four', 'five']
['He said: "Go home."', 'Then he left the']

docs.title: Rhythm of the sentences
docs.text:
sentence_rhythm(lengths, *, messages=MESSAGES)

Gives the rhythm of the sentences from their lengths in words: the mean sents_mean, the standard deviation sents_std, the coefficient of variation sents_cv and the lag-1 autocorrelation of neighbouring lengths sents_autocorr (Yule, 1939). The deviation needs two sentences, the autocorrelation three of unequal lengths, the coefficient of variation a mean above zero; otherwise, and without sentences, a feature is nan.

Parameter Type Default Description lengths list[int] - Lengths of the sentences in words messages dict[str, str] MESSAGES Messages of the errors by key

Lengths that are not a list of integers raise SourceTypeError, a negative length ParameterError.

CodeResult 
from anyts.corpus import sentence_rhythm

{key: round(value, 3) for key, value in sentence_rhythm([4, 8, 2, 7]).items()}

{'sents_mean': 5.25, 'sents_std': 2.754, 'sents_cv': 0.525, 'sents_autocorr': -0.794}

docs.title: Word dispersion
docs.text:
dispersion(words, parts=10, word=None, min_freq=1)

The dispersion of a word is how evenly it is spread over the parts of a text or of a corpus. Frequency does not tell a word occurring once in every chapter from one gathered in a single chapter; the measures of dispersion (Gries 2008, 2020) complement it.

parts is the number of parts of about equal size or the sizes of the parts in order (sentences, paragraphs, chapters, documents of a corpus), adding up to the number of words. Six measures are computed from the frequencies of every word by part; Gries recommends DP as the main one.

Words are compared as they are: case and lemmatization belong to the word extractor.

CodeResult 
from anyts import SentsExtractor, WordsExtractor
from anyts.corpus import dispersion

text = (
    "The cat was at the window and watched the birds. The birds flew away and the cat "
    "fell asleep at the window. Tomorrow the cat will be at the window and watch the birds."
)
we = WordsExtractor(lowercase=True)
words = we.extract(text)
sizes = [len(we.extract(sent)) for sent in SentsExtractor().extract(text)]
sizes
dispersion(words, parts=sizes, word="cat")

# Three equal parts: birds are gathered at the edges of the text
[(d.word, round(d.dp, 2)) for d in dispersion(words, parts=3, min_freq=3)]

[10, 12, 12]
[Dispersion(word='cat', freq=3, dp=0.039215686274509776, dp_norm=0.05555555555555552, juilland_d=0.9374999999999999, carroll_d2=0.9965119062478288, rosengren_s=0.998213770592287, kl_divergence=0.005215975085958165)]
[('the', 0.1), ('cat', 0.02), ('at', 0.02), ('window', 0.02), ('and', 0.02), ('birds', 0.32)]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of the text in order parts int / list[int] 10 Number of parts (from 2 to the number of words) or sizes of the parts word str None Word whose dispersion is needed; None - every word min_freq int 1 Minimum frequency of a word

Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, and no words SourceError. A parts that is neither an integer from 2 to the number of words nor two or more positive integers adding up to it, a word that is not a string and a min_freq that is not an integer raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Result
docs.text:
Dispersion(word, freq, dp, dp_norm, juilland_d, carroll_d2, rosengren_s, kl_divergence)

A list of Dispersion named tuples by descending frequency: the word, its frequency and the measures; pd.DataFrame(result) gives a table.

docs.title: Measures
docs.text:
The measures, the fields of Dispersion, with their names in anyts.constants.DISPERSION_STATS_DESC:

Field Measures Range Higher means dp Deviation of the shares of the occurrences from the shares of the parts 0 to \(1 - \min s_i\) More uneven dp_norm DP over its greatest possible value 0-1 More uneven juilland_d Variation of the relative frequencies by part 0-1 More even carroll_d2 Entropy of the relative frequencies by part 0-1 More even rosengren_s Spread of the occurrences against the sizes of the parts \(\min s_i\) to 1 More even kl_divergence Divergence of the shares of the occurrences from the shares of the parts, in bits 0 to \(-\log_2 \min s_i\) More uneven

Every measure is a function of the module anyts.corpus.dispersion of the frequencies of the word by part and the sizes of the parts. For \(n\) parts of sizes \(n_i\) and shares \(s_i\) of the text, frequencies of the word by part \(v_i\) and a total frequency \(f = \sum v_i\), \(p_i = v_i / n_i\) is the relative frequency in a part:

Parameter Type Default Description frequencies list[int] - Frequencies of the word by part sizes list[int] - Sizes of the parts

For a word of zero frequency every measure is nan.

docs.title: Deviation of proportions DP
docs.text:
dp · Gries (2008)

calc_dp(frequencies, sizes)

How far the shares of the occurrences of the word by part are from the shares of the parts: 0 means the word is spread in proportion to the sizes of the parts, \(1 - s_i\) that it is all in part \(i\).

\[ DP = \frac{1}{2} \sum \left\lvert \frac{v_i}{f} - s_i \right\rvert \]

docs.title: Normalized DP
docs.text:
dp_norm · Lijffijt and Gries (2012)

calc_dp_norm(frequencies, sizes)

DP divided by its greatest possible value, so the maximum is one whatever the split.

\[ \frac{DP}{1 - \min s_i} \]

docs.title: Juilland's D
docs.text:
juilland_d · Juilland and Chang-Rodríguez (1964)

calc_juilland_d(frequencies, sizes)

One less the coefficient of variation \(V\) of the relative frequencies \(p_i\) over its greatest value \(\sqrt{n - 1}\): 1 means even, 0 all in one part. The standard deviation \(\sigma\) is that of the population, as in Gries (2020); Gries (2008) takes the sample one.

\[ 1 - \frac{V}{\sqrt{n - 1}}, \quad V = \frac{\sigma(p)}{\mu(p)} \]

docs.title: Carroll's D2
docs.text:
carroll_d2 · Carroll (1970)

calc_carroll_d2(frequencies, sizes)

The entropy of the distribution of the relative frequencies \(p_i\) over the parts, divided by its greatest value: 1 means even, 0 all in one part.

\[ \frac{H(p)}{\log_2 n} \]

docs.title: Rosengren's S
docs.text:
rosengren_s · Rosengren (1971)

calc_rosengren_s(frequencies, sizes)

1 means the word is spread in proportion to the sizes of the parts; all in part \(i\), it gives \(s_i\), so \(1/n\) in one of \(n\) equal parts.

\[ \frac{(\sum \sqrt{s_i v_i})^2}{f} \]

docs.title: Kullback-Leibler divergence
docs.text:
kl_divergence · Gries (2020)

calc_kl_divergence(frequencies, sizes)

The divergence of the shares of the occurrences of the word by part from the shares of the parts: 0 means in proportion; it grows when the word is gathered in small parts.

\[ \sum \frac{v_i}{f} \log_2 \frac{v_i / f}{s_i} \]

docs.title: Keywords
docs.text:
keyness(target, reference, measure='log_likelihood', min_freq=1, positive=True, top_n=None)

Keyword extraction (keyness) for a target corpus against a reference one: the words that occur significantly more often in the target corpus than in the reference.

Every word gets two values that Gabrielatos and Marchi and Hardie recommend reading together: the log-likelihood \(G^2\) with its p-value (whether there is a difference) and Log Ratio (how large it is), plus the chosen measure score, which sorts the list. The measures of significance (\(G^2\), chi-square, BIC) and ELL, the effect size of \(G^2\), are negative when the word is more frequent in the reference; %DIFF, Log Ratio and the odds ratio are directional by construction.

The reference may be a list of words, a mapping of frequencies (its size is the sum of the counts) or a FrequencyReference. Words are compared as they are: case, lemmatization and stop words belong to the word extractor, and both corpora have to be extracted the same way.

CodeResult 
from anyts import WordsExtractor
from anyts.corpus import keyness

we = WordsExtractor(lowercase=True)
target = we.extract(
    "The cat was at the window and watched the birds. The birds flew away and the cat "
    "fell asleep at the window. Tomorrow the cat will be at the window and watch the birds."
)
reference = we.extract(
    "The dog was on the floor and slept. Then the dog ate and slept again. "
    "Tomorrow the dog will go for a walk."
)

[(k.word, k.freq_target, round(k.g2, 2)) for k in keyness(target, reference, top_n=3)]
[(k.word, round(k.g2, 2)) for k in keyness(target, reference, positive=False, top_n=2)]

[('at', 3, 3.1), ('birds', 3, 3.1), ('cat', 3, 3.1)]
[('dog', -5.45), ('slept', -3.63)]

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description target list[str] / dict[str, int] - Words of the target corpus or their frequencies reference list[str] / dict[str, float] / FrequencyReference - Words of the reference corpus, their frequencies or a reference by frequencies measure str 'log_likelihood' Measure of anyts.constants.KEYNESS_MEASURES for score and the sorting min_freq int 1 Minimum frequency of a keyword in its own corpus positive bool True Positive keywords (more frequent in the target corpus) or negative ones (more frequent in the reference) top_n int None Number of keywords; None - all of them

The parameters and the target corpus are checked by check_keyness_params. A reference that is not a list of strings, a counter or a FrequencyReference raises SourceTypeError, and a negative, nan or infinite frequency of a counter and an empty corpus raise SourceError.

check_keyness_params(measure='log_likelihood', min_freq=1, top_n=None, target=None)

Checks the parameters of keyness before a frequency dictionary is read: it raises ParameterError unless the measure is one of KEYNESS_MEASURES, the minimum frequency is an integer and the number of keywords is None or an integer of at least one. With target it also raises SourceTypeError unless the target corpus is a list of strings or a mapping of strings to whole frequencies, and SourceError for a negative, nan or infinite frequency.

docs.title: Reference by frequencies
docs.text:
FrequencyReference(counts, size, missing=0.0, key=None, keep=None)

A reference corpus described by its frequencies alone, such as a frequency dictionary built from a corpus too large to pass as words:

Field Type Default Description counts dict[str, float] - Frequencies of the keys in the reference corpus size float - Size of the reference corpus in words missing float 0.0 Frequency of a key missing from counts key Callable None Key of a word of the target corpus in counts, such as its lemma; None - the word itself keep Callable None Whether a word of the target corpus is counted; None - every word

Only the words of the target that keep passes are counted, under their key, in the frequencies and in the size alike. A key missing from counts has the frequency missing, such as the least frequency of a dictionary: an upper bound, so its word may be a positive keyword but never a negative one. Negative keywords come only from the keys of counts that keep passes. A frequency is checked as it is read, so a large dictionary is not gone through for positive keywords: one that is not a number raises SourceTypeError, and a negative, nan or infinite one SourceError. A size or a missing that is not a finite number or is negative raises ParameterError, and a key or a keep that cannot be called SourceTypeError.

CodeResult 
from anyts.corpus import FrequencyReference

# Frequencies of the lemmas in a dictionary of a million words
counts = {
    "the": 60_000.0,
    "and": 28_000.0,

docs.title: Measures
docs.text:
The measures of measure by key, with their names and descriptions in anyts.constants.KEYNESS_MEASURES:

Key Measures Range Higher means log_likelihood Significance of the difference of the frequencies Any number A more significant excess in the target corpus chi2 Significance of the difference, with Yates's correction Any number A more significant excess in the target corpus diff Difference of the frequencies per million, in percent of the reference Above −100 A larger excess in the target corpus log_ratio Binary logarithm of the ratio of the frequencies per million Any number A larger excess in the target corpus bic Evidence of the difference: \(G^2\) penalized by the size of the corpora Any number Stronger evidence of an excess in the target corpus, for a word more frequent there ell Effect size of \(G^2\) −1 to 1 as a rule, nan for small expected frequencies A larger excess in the target corpus odds_ratio Ratio of the odds of the word in the corpora 0 to inf, nan if the word fills both corpora Higher odds in the target corpus

Every measure is a function of the module anyts.corpus.keyness of the frequencies of a word and the sizes of the corpora, \(N = c + d\):

Parameter Type Default Description a float - Frequency of the word in the target corpus b float - Frequency of the word in the reference corpus c float - Size of the target corpus d float - Size of the reference corpus

A zero frequency in one of the corpora is replaced with 0.5 for %DIFF, Log Ratio and the odds ratio (Hardie 2014).

docs.title: Log-likelihood
docs.text:
log_likelihood · g2 · p_value · Rayson and Garside (2000)

calc_log_likelihood(a, b, c, d)

The log-likelihood of the frequencies of the word against the expected ones \(E_1\) and \(E_2\); a term of zero frequency is zero. The critical values are anyts.constants.G2_CRITICAL_VALUES: 3.84 for p < 0.05, 6.63 for p < 0.01, 10.83 for p < 0.001, 15.13 for p < 0.0001. The sign is negative when the word is more frequent in the reference.

\[ G^2 = 2 \left(a \ln \frac{a}{E_1} + b \ln \frac{b}{E_2}\right), \quad E_1 = \frac{c\,(a+b)}{N}, \quad E_2 = \frac{d\,(a+b)}{N} \] 
calc_p_value(g2)

The p-value of a \(G^2\) or a chi-square, whatever its sign, by the chi-square distribution with one degree of freedom; an array of values gives an array.

docs.title: Chi-square
docs.text:
chi2

calc_chi2(a, b, c, d)

The chi-square with Yates's correction over the 2×2 contingency table of the word and the other words of each corpus. When the correction exceeds the difference, the statistic is zero. The sign is negative when the word is more frequent in the reference.

\[ \chi^2 = \frac{N\,\max(\lvert a(d-b) - b(c-a) \rvert - N/2,\ 0)^2}{(a+b)(N-a-b)\,c\,d} \]

docs.title: %DIFF
docs.text:
diff · Gabrielatos and Marchi (2011)

calc_diff(a, b, c, d)

The difference of the frequencies \(NF\) per million words, in percent of the frequency in the reference.

\[ \frac{NF_a - NF_b}{NF_b} \cdot 100 \]

docs.title: Log Ratio
docs.text:
log_ratio · Hardie (2014)

calc_log_ratio(a, b, c, d)

The binary logarithm of the ratio of the frequencies \(NF\) per million words: one means the word is twice as frequent in the target corpus.

\[ \log_2 \frac{NF_a}{NF_b} \]

docs.title: BIC
docs.text:
bic · Wilson (2013)

calc_bic(a, b, c, d)

The Bayesian information criterion of \(G^2\). In absolute value above 2 it is positive evidence of a difference, above 6 strong, above 10 very strong; a value of the sign opposite to \(G^2\), when \(\lvert G^2 \rvert < \ln N\), means no evidence, not the opposite direction.

\[ \operatorname{sign}(G^2) \cdot (\lvert G^2 \rvert - \ln N) \]

docs.title: ELL
docs.text:
ell · Johnston, Berry and Mielke (2006)

calc_ell(a, b, c, d)

The effect size of \(G^2\): the share of the greatest possible departure from the expected frequencies \(E_1\) and \(E_2\). It grows without bound as the least expected frequency nears one and is nan when that frequency is at most one (a logarithm of zero or below). The sign is negative when the word is more frequent in the reference.

\[ \frac{G^2}{N \ln \min(E_1, E_2)} \]

docs.title: Odds ratio
docs.text:
odds_ratio

calc_odds_ratio(a, b, c, d)

The ratio of the odds of the word in the two corpora: one means equal odds. A word that fills the whole target corpus gives inf, the whole reference 0, both nan.

\[ \frac{a / (c - a)}{b / (d - b)} \]

docs.title: KWIC concordance
docs.text:
kwic(source, keyword, window=5, by_lemma=False, ignore_case=True, tokenize=None, lemmatize=None, fold=str.lower, join_hyphens=False, sentenize=None)

A KWIC concordance (keyword in context) - every occurrence of a word or a phrase with its context on both sides. Occurrences are found among the words of the text by the word form, ignoring case or respecting it (ignore_case=False), or by the lemma (by_lemma=True); the keyword is lemmatized as a string, so with a lemmatizer a phrase may be written in any form and without one it is given by lemmas. The words of a string and of the keyword come from the tokenizer, those of a Doc from its tokens: a tokenizer that splits a string as the pipeline does finds the same in both. Punctuation and symbols are not words; forms are compared in the composed form of Unicode (NFC), without soft hyphens.

A phrase does not cross the end of a paragraph or a sentence unless the keyword has a final mark or a sentence start in the same place (U.S. Army). A sentence ends at a boundary of a Doc anywhere between the words, an opening mark included, or, without boundaries or with partial ones (has_sents), at a sentence start of the sentence splitter, by default a final mark before whitespace. The context is window words on each side as written, punctuation included; whitespace collapses into one space, and occurrences do not overlap.

CodeResult 
from anyts.corpus import kwic, print_kwic

text = (
    "The cat was at the window and watched the birds. The birds flew away and the cat "
    "fell asleep at the window. Tomorrow the cat will be at the window and watch the birds."
)
lines = kwic(text, "window", window=3)
lines[0]
print_kwic(lines, width=20)

lemmas = {"watched": "watch", "birds": "bird"}
[
    line.keyword
    for line in kwic(
        text,
        "watch the bird",
        by_lemma=True,
        lemmatize=lambda word, tokens: [lemmas.get(word, word)],
    )
]

Concordance(start=19, end=25, left='was at the', keyword='window', right='and watched the')
          was at the  window  and watched the
       asleep at the  window  . Tomorrow the cat
           be at the  window  and watch the
['watched the birds', 'watch the birds']

docs.title: For library developers
docs.text:
Language hooks of the parameters

The language enters through five parameters:

Parameter Type Default Description tokenize Callable None The words of a string and of the keyword as triples of the start, the end and the text; a run of word characters by default lemmatize Callable None The lemmas of a word, given its text and its tokens in a Doc (none for a string and the keyword), or one lemma as a string; a word matches when one of its lemmas is one of those of the keyword fold Callable str.lower The folding of a word form (with ignore_case) or a lemma before the comparison, such as the letters a language takes for the same join_hyphens bool False Join the parts of the hyphenated words of a Doc the tokenizer split (iter_doc_units); the default tokenizer then keeps them whole in a string and in the keyword too sentenize Callable None The sentences of a string, of the keyword and of the text of a Doc without boundaries or with partial ones (has_sents) as triples of the start, the end and the text; a final mark before whitespace by default

A tokenize that does not give the words in order as triples of integer bounds within the string and a string raises SourceTypeError, and so does a sentenize whose triples do not lie within it; the sentences may come in any order. The words of a Doc are its tokens without a byte order mark at the start. By default the lemmas of a word are the word itself and, for a one-token word of a Doc with lemmas, the lemma of the model: a word is found by its own form, and a Doc of a pipeline with a lemmatizer by its lemmas.

docs.title: Stylometry
docs.text: Measures of stylometry and authorship attribution: distances between texts by the frequencies of the most frequent words (Burrows's Delta and its variants, as in stylo), markers of preferred and avoided words (Zeta), Kilgarriff's chi-square distance between corpora and the Mendenhall curve. The functions work on lists of units of a text: lower-case word forms (the usual choice for Delta), lemmas or character N-grams - case and lemmatization belong to the extractors.

docs.title: Burrows's Delta
docs.text:
frequency_table(corpus, n_mfw=100, culling=0.0)

Builds the table of relative frequencies of a corpus, a dictionary "name of a text → units": rows are the texts, columns the n_mfw most frequent units by descending mean relative frequency (alphabetically when equal); culling keeps the units that occur in at least the given share of the texts, as in stylo.

Parameter Type Default Description corpus dict[str, list[str]] - Units of the texts by the names of the texts n_mfw int 100 Number of the most frequent units; None - all of them culling float 0.0 Smallest share of the texts a unit occurs in

A corpus that is not a mapping of lists of strings raises SourceTypeError; an empty corpus, a text without units and no unit left after culling raise SourceError, and an n_mfw that is not an integer of at least one and a culling that is not a number within [0, 1] ParameterError.

z_scores(table)

Standardizes the columns of a table of frequencies with the sample standard deviation, like scale() of R; a column with the same frequency in every text gives zeros.

Parameter Type Default Description table DataFrame - Table of relative frequencies 
delta(corpus, n_mfw=100, variant='burrows', culling=0.0)

Computes a symmetric matrix of distances from the z-scores (a DataFrame with the names of the texts); at least three texts are needed - with two, the z-scores degenerate to ±1/√2 and the distances do not depend on the frequencies.

The variants (anyts.constants.DELTA_VARIANTS), with the formulas of the sources of stylo; \(n\) is the number of units, \(z_A\) and \(z_B\) the vectors of z-scores of the texts:

Variant Key Formula Source Burrows's Delta burrows \(\frac{1}{n} \sum_i \lvert z_{A,i} - z_{B,i} \rvert\) Burrows (2002), dist.delta Quadratic Delta quadratic \(\frac{1}{n} \sqrt{\sum_i (z_{A,i} - z_{B,i})^2}\) Argamon (2008), dist.argamon Eder's Delta eder \(\sum_i \frac{n - i + 2}{n} \lvert z_{A,i} - z_{B,i} \rvert\), \(i\) - rank of the unit by frequency Eder, dist.eder Cosine Delta cosine \(1 - \frac{z_A \cdot z_B}{\lVert z_A \rVert \lVert z_B \rVert}\) Smith and Aldridge (2011), Evert et al. (2015), dist.wurzburg

Cosine Delta clusters the texts by author best in the experiments of Evert et al. The usual number of units is 100 to 500 most frequent words, 100-200 for character N-grams.

Parameter Type Default Description corpus dict[str, list[str]] - Units of the texts by the names of the texts n_mfw int 100 Number of the most frequent units; None - all of them variant str 'burrows' Variant of Delta of anyts.constants.DELTA_VARIANTS culling float 0.0 Smallest share of the texts a unit occurs in

The corpus, n_mfw and culling raise the errors of frequency_table; fewer than three texts raise SourceError, and an unknown variant ParameterError.

delta_profiles(reference, samples, n_mfw=100, variant='burrows', culling=0.0, statistics=None)

Distances by Delta for authorship attribution. The most frequent units, the culling and the statistics of the z-scores come from the reference texts (the profiles of the authors) or from a separate set statistics, such as training windows when the profiles are too few to estimate the spread of the frequencies; the texts under test samples get the same units and scaling. The result is the distances from the samples (rows) to the references (columns); the nearest reference is the presumed author. Unlike in delta, a sample affects neither the units nor the scaling, so its result does not depend on the other samples.

Parameter Type Default Description reference dict[str, list[str]] - Units of the reference texts by the names of the texts samples dict[str, list[str]] - Units of the texts under test by the names of the texts n_mfw int 100 Number of the most frequent units; None - all of them variant str 'burrows' Variant of Delta of anyts.constants.DELTA_VARIANTS culling float 0.0 Smallest share of the texts a unit occurs in statistics dict[str, list[str]] None Texts of the units and of the statistics of the scaling; None - the reference texts

The corpora, n_mfw and culling raise the errors of frequency_table; fewer than three texts for the statistics raise SourceError, and an unknown variant ParameterError.

CodeResult 
from anyts import WordsExtractor
from anyts.corpus import delta, delta_profiles, frequency_table

texts = {
    "A": (
        "The cat was at the window and watched the birds. "
        "The birds flew away and the cat slept at the window."
    ),
    "B": "The dog was on the floor and slept. Then the dog ate and slept again on the floor.",
    "C": "Tomorrow the cat will come back to the window and watch the birds, but the dog will sleep.",
}
we = WordsExtractor(lowercase=True)
corpus = {name: we.extract(text) for name, text in texts.items()}

frequency_table(corpus, n_mfw=5).round(3)
delta(corpus, n_mfw=5).round(3)
delta(corpus, n_mfw=5, variant="cosine").round(3)

sample = {"?": we.extract("The cat woke up at the window and watched the birds again.")}
delta_profiles(corpus, sample, n_mfw=5).round(3)

docs.title: Zeta
docs.text:
zeta(target, comparison, segment_size=2000, top_n=None)

Markers of preferred and avoided words after Burrows (2007) and Craig and Kinney (2009). Every text of both corpora is split into segments of about segment_size words (the length over the size rounded half up, at least one segment); \(DP\) is the share of the segments of a corpus with the word. Zeta is \(DP_{target} - DP_{comparison}\), from −1 to 1 (zeta.craig in stylo; the classic Zeta of Craig, \(DP_{target} + (1 - DP_{comparison})\), is greater by one); the logarithmic Zeta is \(\log_2 \frac{DP_{target}}{DP_{comparison}}\) (Schöch et al. 2018), a zero share replaced by half a segment. The list goes from the words the target corpus prefers to those it avoids.

Parameter Type Default Description target list[str] / list[list[str]] - Words of the target corpus - one text or a list of texts comparison list[str] / list[list[str]] - Words of the comparison corpus segment_size int 2000 Size of a segment in words top_n int None Number of words from the start of the list; None - all of them

The result is a list of ZetaScore(word, dp_target, dp_comparison, zeta, log_zeta) named tuples by descending Zeta, by descending logarithmic Zeta and alphabetically when equal. A corpus that is neither a list of strings nor a list of such lists raises SourceTypeError, and a corpus without words SourceError; a segment_size or a top_n that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

CodeResult 
from anyts.corpus import zeta

zeta(corpus["A"], corpus["B"], segment_size=5, top_n=2)
zeta(corpus["A"], corpus["B"], segment_size=5)[-1]

[ZetaScore(word='at', dp_target=0.5, dp_comparison=0.0, zeta=0.5, log_zeta=2.0), ZetaScore(word='birds', dp_target=0.5, dp_comparison=0.0, zeta=0.5, log_zeta=2.0)]

docs.title: Kilgarriff's chi-square
docs.text:
kilgarriff_chi2(words_a, words_b, n_mfw=500)

The distance between two corpora after Kilgarriff (2001): for the n_mfw most frequent words of the joint corpus the expected frequencies in the corpora are proportional to their sizes, \(\chi^2 = \sum (O - E)^2 / E\) over the words and both corpora. The greater the value, the more the corpora differ; it grows with the size of the corpora, so only pairs of equal sizes are comparable.

Parameter Type Default Description words_a list[str] - Words of the first corpus words_b list[str] - Words of the second corpus n_mfw int 500 Number of the most frequent words of the joint corpus

Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, a corpus without words SourceError, and an n_mfw that is not an integer of at least one ParameterError.

CodeResult 
from anyts.corpus import kilgarriff_chi2

round(kilgarriff_chi2(corpus["A"], corpus["B"], n_mfw=5), 3)

4.113

The shares of the words of every length in characters by ascending length (Mendenhall 1887), a profile of the author comparable between texts whatever their size.

The Jensen-Shannon distance with base 2 between the Mendenhall curves of two texts, from 0 (the distributions coincide) to 1.

{length: round(share, 3) for length, share in mendenhall_curve(corpus["A"]).items()}

docs.title: Character N-gram extraction
docs.text:
CharNgramsExtractor(n=2, lowercase=False, within_words=False, tokenizer=None)

A class for extracting character N-grams from a text - sequences of N characters taken with a sliding window over the string. Character N-grams are a standard feature of stylometry and authorship attribution (Stamatatos 2009) and can replace words in measures such as Burrows's Delta.

Whitespace runs are collapsed into a single space, punctuation marks are kept. With within_words=True N-grams do not cross word boundaries: the text is split into words by the tokenizer, punctuation is dropped, and words shorter than N yield no N-grams.

Raises:

  • ParameterError - an n that is not an integer of at least one, a lowercase or within_words that is not a bool.
CodeResult 
from anyts import CharNgramsExtractor

text = "The cat slept  on the sill, and the dog - on the floor."

ce = CharNgramsExtractor(n=3, lowercase=True)
ce.extract(text)[:6]
CharNgramsExtractor(n=4, lowercase=True, within_words=True).extract(text)

('the', 'he ', 'e c', ' ca', 'cat', 'at ')
('slep', 'lept', 'sill', 'floo', 'loor')

docs.title: For library developers
docs.text:
Language hooks of a subclass

The default word tokenizer for within_words is the method tokenize(text), which a language library overrides in a subclass. In the core it is the default tokenizer of WordsExtractor: a word character \w followed by word characters, combining marks, zero-width joiners and non-joiners and soft hyphens, so don't gives the words don and t. The messages of its errors come from the class attribute messages, MESSAGES by default.

docs.title: Sentence extraction
docs.text:
SentsExtractor(tokenizer=None, min_len=0, max_len=0)

A class for extracting sentences from a text.

Raises:

  • ParameterError - a length bound that is not an integer, a negative bound, a minimum above the maximum.
CodeResult 
from anyts import SentsExtractor

SentsExtractor().extract('It rains. Does it? He said "Yes!" Then he left.')

('It rains.', 'Does it?', 'He said "Yes!"', 'Then he left.')

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description tokenizer Pattern / Callable None Tokenizer or regular expression; by default the sentenize method min_len int 0 Minimum length of an extracted sentence in characters, 0 for no bound max_len int 0 Maximum length of an extracted sentence in characters, 0 for no bound

Note

A regular expression as the tokenizer is a separator for re.split. A blank line - a line break, optional whitespace and another line break - ends a sentence of any tokenizer: the text is split at blank lines first and every part goes to the tokenizer, so a heading or a paragraph without a final mark is a sentence of its own, and so is a part without words, such as a line of asterisks, which the statistics leave out. The sentences are stripped of whitespace at the edges before the length bounds, and empty ones are dropped.

Note

A spaCy pipeline can be passed as the tokenizer: tokenizer=lambda text: (sent.text for sent in nlp(text).sents).

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
extract(text) extracts sentences from a text.

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text string

A text that is not a string and a tokenizer that cannot be called or does not return strings raise SourceTypeError.

CodeResult 
import re

SentsExtractor().extract("What is new\n\nFaster import\nFewer bugs\n\nThanks for reading!")
SentsExtractor(tokenizer=re.compile(r", ")).extract("Rain today, sun tomorrow")

('What is new', 'Faster import\nFewer bugs', 'Thanks for reading!')
('Rain today', 'sun tomorrow')

docs.title: Sentences of the parts of a text
docs.text:
iter_part_sents(iter_sents, text)

Runs the splitter iter_sents on every part of a text between blank lines (BLANK_LINE) and gives the sentences at their positions in the whole text, so that a blank line ends a sentence whatever the splitter, as in SentsExtractor.

Parameter Type Default Description iter_sents Callable - Splitter giving the start, the end and the text of every sentence of a string text str - Text string

A text that is not a string raises SourceTypeError, and so does an iter_sents that cannot be called or does not give the sentences of a part in order, as triples of integer bounds within it and a string.

CodeResult 
import re

from anyts.extractors import iter_part_sents


def periods(text):
    return [(m.start(), m.end(), m.group()) for m in re.finditer(r"[^.\s][^.]*\.?", text)]


list(iter_part_sents(periods, "One. Two\n\nThree."))

[(0, 4, 'One.'), (5, 8, 'Two'), (10, 16, 'Three.')]

docs.title: Ready sentences
docs.text:
FixedSentsExtractor(sents)

A SentsExtractor that gives the sentences it was made with for any text, so a class that takes a sentence extractor gets known sentences without splitting the text again.

Parameter Type Default Description sents list[str] - Sentences

Sentences that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError.

from anyts.extractors import FixedSentsExtractor

FixedSentsExtractor(["It rains.", "Yes!"]).extract("any text")
