docs.title: For library developers
docs.text:
Language hooks of a subclass

The default tokenizer is the method sentenize(text), which a language library overrides in a subclass. In the core it splits the text at whitespace after ., !, ? or …, optionally followed by a closing quote or bracket; it knows no abbreviations, so e.g. this is two sentences. A piece without words, such as the dots of a spaced ellipsis . . . or a lone !, stays with the sentence before it, or with the one after it at the start of the text. The messages of its errors come from the class attribute messages, MESSAGES by default.

docs.title: Word extraction
docs.text:
WordsExtractor(tokenizer=None, filter_punct=True, filter_nums=False, use_lexemes=False, stopwords=None, lowercase=False, ngram_range=(1, 1), min_len=0, max_len=0)

A class for extracting words from a text.

Raises:

  • ParameterError - an ngram_range that is not a pair of integers or whose lower bound is below one or above the upper one, a length bound that is not an integer, a negative bound, a minimum above the maximum, a switch that is not a bool;
  • SourceTypeError - stop words that are not a collection of strings.
CodeResult 
from anyts import WordsExtractor

text = "Better 100 friends than 100 dollars"

we = WordsExtractor(lowercase=True, stopwords=["than"], filter_nums=True, ngram_range=(1, 2))
we.extract(text)

('better', 'friends', 'dollars', 'better_friends', 'friends_dollars')

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description tokenizer Pattern / Callable None Tokenizer or regular expression; by default the tokenize method filter_punct bool True Filter punctuation marks filter_nums bool False Filter numbers matched by number_pattern use_lexemes bool False Use word lemmas of the lemmatize method stopwords Collection[str] None Stop words, compared case-insensitively lowercase bool False Convert words to lower case ngram_range tuple[int, int] (1, 1) Lower and upper bound of the N-gram size min_len int 0 Minimum length of an extracted word in characters, 0 for no bound max_len int 0 Maximum length of an extracted word in characters, 0 for no bound

Note

A regular expression as the tokenizer is a separator for re.split. The filters are applied in order: punctuation, numbers, lemmatization, lower case, stop words, word length. A punctuation mark is a token of marks and symbols only, multi-character ones included: ?!, --, …, € (anyts.utils.is_punctuation). Empty and whitespace tokens are dropped before the filters. N-grams join the words with _.

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
extract(text) extracts words from a text.

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text string

A text that is not a string and a tokenizer that cannot be called or does not return strings raise SourceTypeError.

get_most_common(n=10) returns the top words of the text as a list of (word, frequency) pairs, the most frequent first.

Parameter Type Default Description n int 10 Number of top words

A number that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

Warning

The method must be called after words have been extracted with extract.

CodeResult 
we = WordsExtractor(lowercase=True)
we.extract("The cat saw the dog and the bird")
we.get_most_common(2)

('the', 'cat', 'saw', 'the', 'dog', 'and', 'the', 'bird')
[('the', 3), ('cat', 1)]

docs.title: For library developers
Basic statistics
docs.text:
BasicStats(source, sents_extractor=None, words_extractor=None, normalize=False, complex_syl_factor=3, long_word_letter_factor=7)

The basic statistics of a text: the counts of its sentences, words, characters, syllables and punctuation marks and the distributions of its words. The data source is a text or a Doc object of spaCy. Letters are counted by str.isalpha, so digits, hyphens and marks inside a word are not letters.

The words and the sentences of a string come from the extractors. A Doc gives its tokens as words, without punctuation marks and symbols such as € or %, and its boundaries as sentences, or those of the sentence extractor when it has none or only partial ones (has_sents); an extractor given is used on its text instead. A blank line ends a sentence of a string and of a Doc without boundaries; a Doc with boundaries does so when its pipeline has start_sents_after_blank_lines (registered by a language library under its own name) before the parser, senter or sentencizer. A sentence without words, such as punctuation alone, is not counted.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is neither a string nor a Doc, an extractor of another type;
  • SourceError - a source without words;
  • ParameterError - a threshold that is not an integer of at least one, a normalize that is not a bool.

A subclass with the syllables of a language - here the groups of vowels, a rough rule for English.

CodeResult 
import re

from anyts.basic_stats import BasicStats


class Stats(BasicStats):
    def count_syllables(self, word):
        return len(re.findall(r"[aeiouy]+", word, re.IGNORECASE))


bs = Stats("The cat sat on the mat. A beautiful day!")
bs.print_stats()

docs.title: Punctuation marks
docs.text:
count_punctuations(text, marks=PUNCTUATION_MARKS, dash_pattern=DASH_PATTERN)

Counts punctuation marks by type, the distribution of c_punctuations: commas, periods, question and exclamation marks, ellipses, colons, semicolons, dashes, hyphens, guillemets, quotation marks, parentheses and other marks. Dashes typed with hyphens (dash_pattern) are counted first, then ellipses - …, three or more periods, or two after ? and !, one mark whose periods are not counted as periods (Who?.. is a question and an ellipsis) - then each mark by its type in marks; any other character of the Unicode categories P and S is another mark (§, €, °).

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text string marks dict[str, str] PUNCTUATION_MARKS Type of every mark, among PUNCTUATION_TYPES dash_pattern Pattern DASH_PATTERN Dashes typed with hyphens

A mark of marks that is not a single character or has an unknown type raises ParameterError; a text that is not a string, marks that are not a mapping and a dash_pattern that is not a compiled regular expression raise SourceTypeError.

In the core the types are anyts.constants.PUNCTUATION_TYPES, and marks and dash_pattern are PUNCTUATION_MARKS and DASH_PATTERN of anyts.basic_stats. The marks count ¿ and ¡ as question and exclamation marks (¿So? has two), —, – and the horizontal bar ― as dashes, «» as guillemets and "“”‘’ as quotation marks; a hyphen inside a word, before a digit or at a line break inside a word is a hyphen (well-known, -5). A dash typed with hyphens is a run of two or more hyphens, or a hyphen after whitespace, a closing mark or at the start of a line, before a space of a line (a Unicode separator such as the no-break space, or a tab: SPACES) or the end of the text, or between a letter and an opening or a closing mark (--Hello --said John, - They left - he said).

CodeResult 
from anyts.basic_stats import count_punctuations

counts = count_punctuations('"Well..." - he said - "a well-known cat?!"')
{kind: count for kind, count in counts.items() if count}

{'question': 1, 'exclamation': 1, 'ellipsis': 1, 'dash': 2, 'hyphen': 1, 'straight_quotes': 4}

docs.title: Dashes typed with hyphens
docs.text:
dash_pattern(conjunctions=(), hanging_before_comma=False)

Builds the dash_pattern of count_punctuations. A hanging hyphen glued to a letter or a digit and carried on to a later word (pre- and post-war, 5- and 10-year) stays a hyphen before spaces of a line and one of the conjunctions, case ignored, and with hanging_before_comma before a comma (two-, three- and four-year). A language whose dialogue closes a line with a hyphen before a comma (-Come -he said-, and left) leaves hanging_before_comma off. Without the parameters the pattern is DASH_PATTERN.

Parameter Type Default Description conjunctions Collection[str] () Conjunctions after a hanging hyphen hanging_before_comma bool False Take a hyphen between a letter and a comma for a hanging one

Conjunctions that are not a collection of strings raise SourceTypeError, and an empty conjunction ParameterError.

CodeResult 
from anyts.basic_stats import count_punctuations, dash_pattern

text = "pre- and post-war, two-, three- and four-year - he said"
counts = count_punctuations(text, dash_pattern=dash_pattern(["and"], hanging_before_comma=True))
counts["dash"], counts["hyphen"]

(1, 5)

docs.text:
Language hooks of a subclass

A language library subclasses BasicStats:

Hook Kind Description count_syllables(word) method The syllables of a word; abstract sents_extractor_class, words_extractor_class class attributes The extractors used when none is given; SentsExtractor and WordsExtractor by default join_hyphens class attribute Join the parts of the hyphenated words of a Doc (iter_doc_words); False by default count_punctuations(text) method The punctuation marks by type; count_punctuations of the module by default stats_desc class attribute The counts of get_stats with their descriptions for print_stats; anyts.constants.BASIC_STATS_DESC by default

The other hooks, stats_headers, level_scales and messages, come from Stats. The thresholds of the complex and the long words are parameters; a library sets its own defaults in its __init__ and passes them on.

docs.title: Cohesion statistics
docs.text:
CohesionStats(source, sents_extractor=None, connectors=None)

The cohesion statistics of a text in the manner of Coh-Metrix: the overlap of the sentences, the givenness, the temporal cohesion and the connectors of a dictionary. The sentences are compared by lemmas. The data source is a Doc object of spaCy with the parts of speech and the lemmas, split into sentences by its boundaries, or by the sentence extractor over its text when one is given or the Doc has none.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - an extractor of another type, a source that is not a Doc, connectors that are not a dictionary of phrases and pairs of strings;
  • SourceError - a source without parts of speech, lemmas or words;
  • ParameterError - an unknown class or kind of a connector.
CodeResult 
import spacy
from spacy.tokens import Doc

from anyts.cohesion_stats import CohesionStats


class English(CohesionStats):
    @classmethod
    def load_connectors(cls):
        return {"however": ("adversative", "secondary")}


# The cat slept. However, the cat woke.
doc = Doc(
    spacy.blank("en").vocab,
    words=["The", "cat", "slept", ".", "However", ",", "the", "cat", "woke", "."],
    spaces=[True, True, False, True, False, True, True, True, False, False],
    pos=["DET", "NOUN", "VERB", "PUNCT", "ADV", "PUNCT", "DET", "NOUN", "VERB", "PUNCT"],
    lemmas=["the", "cat", "sleep", ".", "however", ",", "the", "cat", "wake", "."],
    morphs=["", "", "Aspect=Perf|Tense=Past", "", "", "", "", "", "Aspect=Perf|Tense=Past", ""],
    sent_starts=[True, False, False, False, True, False, False, False, False, False],
)
stats = English(doc)
stats.print_stats()

docs.title: Binary overlap
docs.text:
noun_overlap_adjacent · noun_overlap_all · argument_overlap_adjacent · argument_overlap_all · content_overlap_adjacent · content_overlap_all · Coh-Metrix

calc_overlap(sets, adjacent=True)

The binary overlap of Coh-Metrix (CRFNO1, CRFAO1, CRFSO1 over the adjacent pairs, CRFNOa, CRFAOa, CRFSOa over all of them): the share of the pairs of sentences that share at least one element; nan for a text shorter than two sentences.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of pairs sharing an element}}{\textrm{Number of pairs}} \] Parameter Type Default Description sets list[set[str]] - Elements of every sentence adjacent bool True Count the adjacent pairs only, otherwise all the pairs

docs.title: Proportional overlap
docs.text:
content_overlap_prop_adjacent · content_overlap_prop_all · Coh-Metrix

calc_proportional_overlap(sets, adjacent=True)

The proportional overlap of Coh-Metrix (CRFCWO1, CRFCWOa): the Dice coefficient of a pair of sentences (dice) averaged over the pairs; nan for a text shorter than two sentences.

\[ \frac{1}{\textrm{Number of pairs}} \sum_{(A, B)} \textrm{Dice}(A, B) \] Parameter Type Default Description sets list[set[str]] - Elements of every sentence adjacent bool True Count the adjacent pairs only, otherwise all the pairs 
dice(first, second)

The Dice coefficient of two sets, 0 for two empty sets.

\[ \frac{2 \times |A \cap B|}{|A| + |B|} \] Parameter Type Default Description first frozenset[str] - First set second frozenset[str] - Second set

docs.title: Overlap with the next sentences and paragraphs
docs.text:
noun_overlap_2_sent · argument_overlap_2_sent · content_overlap_2_sent · noun_overlap_para · argument_overlap_para · content_overlap_para · TAACO

The adjacent overlap of TAACO, by the lemmas of the nouns, of the arguments and of the content words: the share of the distinct lemmas of a sentence repeated in one of the next two sentences (adjacent_overlap_2_*_sent), and of a paragraph repeated in the next paragraph (adjacent_overlap_*_para), over all the sentences or paragraphs that have them (calc_forward_overlap). Unlike the binary overlap, a pair of segments counts by the share of the lemmas they share. A paragraph is a part of the text between blank lines that holds words; a word that carries paragraph_start opens one, inside a sentence too, as when a parser joins a heading to the next sentence.

calc_forward_overlap(sets, span=1)

The share of the elements of a segment repeated in the next ones: the distinct elements of every segment with span segments after it that one of these segments holds, over the distinct elements of those segments; nan for no more segments than span or for segments without elements.

\[ \frac{\sum_{i=1}^{n-k} |A_i \cap (A_{i+1} \cup \dots \cup A_{i+k})|}{\sum_{i=1}^{n-k} |A_i|} \] Parameter Type Default Description sets list[set[str]] - Elements of every segment span int 1 Number \(k\) of the next segments a segment is compared with

Segments that are a string, a Doc, an iterator or a segment that is not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, a span that is not an integer above 0 ParameterError.

calc_repetition(sents)

The repetition of the tense and of the aspect of Coh-Metrix (SMTEMP): the share of the adjacent pairs of sentences whose verbs have the same dominant value of the feature; a pair where one of the sentences has no verb with the feature is skipped, and without a single such pair the value is nan.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of pairs with the same dominant value}}{\textrm{Number of pairs with the feature}} \] Parameter Type Default Description sents list[list[str]] - Values of the feature of the verbs of every sentence 
dominant(values)

The dominant value: the most frequent one, the first of the equally frequent; None for an empty list.

Parameter Type Default Description values list[str] - Values

docs.title: Connectors
docs.text:
connectors · connectors_inter · connectors_intra · connectors_<class> · connectors_<kind>

The occurrences of the connectors found in every sentence by the matcher of connector_matcher_class, per 1000 words. An inter-sentential connector links a sentence to the ones before: it opens a sentence, unless the matcher takes it for a subordinator (is_subordinator), whose clause or phrase belongs to the same sentence; the others are intra-sentential. Every class and kind of the matcher gives a density: connectors_causal, connectors_adversative, connectors_concessive, connectors_temporal, connectors_additive, connectors_conditional, connectors_reformulative, connectors_primary and connectors_secondary by default.

\[ 1000 \cdot \frac{\textrm{Number of connectors}}{\textrm{Number of words}} \]

docs.title: Connector matcher
docs.text:
ConnectorMatcher(connectors)

The search of the connectors (discourse markers: because, however, on the other hand) of a dictionary in the sentences of a text. The dictionary gives the class of every connector - causal, adversative, concessive, temporal, additive, conditional or reformulative (CONNECTOR_CLASSES) - and its kind, primary or secondary (CONNECTOR_KINDS). A connector is matched by the normalized forms of its words, the longest one at every position, without overlaps; a period or a hyphen inside a connector may be split off by the tokenizer (e.g. as e, g). An occurrence is a Connector: the number of the sentence sent, the positions start and end of its words, the connector text as the dictionary writes it, its class cls and kind kind.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a dictionary that is not a mapping of a phrase to a pair of strings;
  • ParameterError - an unknown class or kind.

find(words, sent_index, pos, breaks, blocked) returns the occurrences of the connectors in a sentence in the order of its words. The words are those of one sentence without punctuation, the first one its start. With the parts of speech, a one-word connector counts only with one of pos_tags or of pos_extra for its form, never after one of not_after_pos, and with one of start_only_pos only at the start of the sentence; a word without a part of speech (None) passes. Without the parts of speech the rules that read them are skipped. The positions of the punctuation marks breaks cut a connector off its neighbours: a rule does not read a word across a mark, so in so, the end the word after the comma neither blocks nor lets the connector count, unless the connector is one of read_through_marks, and a mark between the words of a connector of split_by_marks makes it none; without them the words are read as adjacent. No connector starts at a word of blocked, which a language rules out by more than the words and their parts of speech, such as its parse.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of the sentence sent_index int 0 Number of the sentence, written into the occurrences pos list[str] None Parts of speech of the words breaks set[int] None Positions of the words a punctuation mark stands before blocked set[int] None Positions of the words no connector starts at

Words that are not a list of strings and parts of speech that are not a list of strings and None (the tags token.pos_ of spaCy, not the numbers token.pos) and positions that are not a collection raise SourceTypeError, a number of the sentence or a position that is not an integer, a position of a mark that is not that of a word after the first, a blocked position that is not that of a word and parts of speech not as many as the words ParameterError.

CodeResult 
from anyts.cohesion_stats import ConnectorMatcher


class Matcher(ConnectorMatcher):
    blocked_after = {"before": frozenset({"the"})}
    not_after_pos = frozenset({"DET"})


matcher = Matcher(
    {
        "however": ("adversative", "secondary"),
        "before": ("temporal", "primary"),
        "and": ("additive", "primary"),
        "on the other hand": ("adversative", "secondary"),
    }
)
matcher.find("On the other hand he left before the end".split())
matcher.find(["The", "before", "and", "after"], pos=["DET", "ADV", "CCONJ", "ADV"])

[Connector(sent=0, start=0, end=4, text='on the other hand', cls='adversative', kind='secondary')]
[Connector(sent=0, start=2, end=3, text='and', cls='additive', kind='primary')]

is_subordinator(connector, pos=None) checks whether an occurrence of a connector ties its clause or phrase to its own sentence: a connector of subordinators, or a one-word connector whose part of speech pos is SCONJ or ADP, but none of parcellation. The clause of a subordinating conjunction and the phrase of a preposition belong to the sentence of the connector wherever it stands, so a subordinator opening a sentence (when he came, ..., despite the rain, ...) does not link it to the ones before. A connector that is not a Connector raises SourceTypeError.

docs.title: For library developers
docs.text:
Language hooks of a subclass

A language library subclasses CohesionStats. By default the words and their features are read from a Doc by Universal Dependencies, and there are no connectors:

Hook Kind Description analyze(source) method Words of the sentences of a source as CohesionWord: the word, its lemma, its part of speech, whether it is a noun, a pronoun, a demonstrative, an argument and a content word, its tense, mood and aspect, whether a punctuation mark stands before it (break_before, which the rules of the connectors do not read through), whether no connector starts at it (connector_blocked, by a rule of the parse such as an if of an indirect question) and whether a blank line stands before it (paragraph_start); by default those of a Doc, sentence by sentence (doc_units), with the features of word_info; the default marks the words after a blank line of the Doc; a library that reads a string or a Doc without these annotations overrides it doc_units(doc) method Words of the sentences of a Doc as lists of tokens: by its boundaries, or by the extractor over its text (split_doc_units of anyts.utils) word_info(unit) method Features of a word of a Doc; by default a noun is NOUN or PROPN, a pronoun PRON or a possessive, demonstrative or personal determiner, a demonstrative carries PronType=Dem, an argument is NOUN, PROPN or PRON, a content word one of anyts.constants.CONTENT_UD_POS and no demonstrative, and the tense, the mood and the aspect are the features Tense, Mood and Aspect; a library sets connector_blocked where its parse rules a connector out load_connectors() class method Dictionary of the connectors of the language, class and kind by connector; empty by default connector_matcher() class method Matcher of that dictionary, built once for a class and shared by its instances and by searches outside the statistics connector_matcher_class class attribute Class that finds the connectors with the context rules of the language; ConnectorMatcher by default. A matcher with other classes or kinds gives other connectors_* attributes, so the subclass sets its own stats_desc too temporal_features class attribute Features of the verbs whose repetitions make the temporal cohesion: a tuple of one or more distinct ones of tense, mood and aspect (TEMPORAL_FEATURES), checked when the class is defined; tense and aspect by default, as in Coh-Metrix sents_extractor_class, join_hyphens class attributes Sentence extractor of a Doc without boundaries, joining of the hyphenated words of a Doc stats_desc, stats_headers class attributes Statistics of get_stats with their descriptions (COHESION_STATS_DESC by default), headers of the columns for print_stats messages class attribute Messages of the errors by key; MESSAGES by default

The parameters of a library - its model of a string, its word extractor - go to the constructor of its subclass, which keeps them for its analyze. An analyze that does not give sentences of CohesionWord objects raises SourceTypeError.

Rules of a connector matcher

The rules of a language are class attributes of a subclass, empty by default apart from pos_tags:

Hook Kind Description normalize(text) method Normalized form of a word and of a connector; the lower case by default blocked_after, blocked_before class attributes Words after or before a connector, by its text, that make it no connector (before the end) blocked_after_pos class attribute Parts of speech of the word after a connector, by its text, that make it no connector not_at_start class attribute Connectors that do not count at the start of a sentence, where they open a reply (Well, ...) only_after class attribute Connectors that count inside a sentence only after these words read_through_marks class attribute Connectors whose rules read the words before and after them through a punctuation mark: a comma always separates a question word from the verb before it (asked, why) split_by_marks class attribute Connectors of several words that a punctuation mark between their words makes no connector pos_tags, pos_extra class attributes Parts of speech of a one-word connector, CONNECTOR_POS of Universal Dependencies by default, and those allowed for a word on top of them not_after_pos class attribute Parts of speech of the previous word that make a one-word connector no connector (a determiner: the before and the after) start_only_pos class attribute Parts of speech of a one-word connector that counts only at the start of a sentence (a capitalized connector tagged as a proper noun) subordinators class attribute Connectors that are subordinating conjunctions or prepositions besides the one-word ones tagged SCONJ or ADP (as soon as, in spite of), for is_subordinator parcellation class attribute Connectors that are no subordinators whatever their part of speech: a sentence they open is linked to the one before (parcellation), for is_subordinator classes, kinds class attributes Classes and kinds of the dictionary; CONNECTOR_CLASSES and CONNECTOR_KINDS by default. The names inter and intra (CONNECTOR_PLACES) belong to the densities by place of CohesionStats and raise ParameterError when the class is defined messages class attribute Messages of the errors by key; MESSAGES by default

The words of the lists and the keys of pos_extra are normalized forms; the other lists are keyed by the connector, and a connector of the dictionary finds its rules by its normalized form, however either of them writes it. A rule that is not a collection of strings, or a mapping of strings to them, raises SourceTypeError when the class is defined.

Parameter Type Default Description words Iterable[str] - Words of the text: a sequence or an iterator of strings window_len int 50 Window size for MATTR and segment size for MSTTR (MATTR_WINDOW_LEN) mtld_threshold float 0.72 TTR threshold for MTLD, MA-MTLD and MTLD-W (MTLD_TTR_THRESHOLD) mtld_min_len int 10 Minimum factor length for MTLD, MA-MTLD and MTLD-W (MTLD_MIN_LEN) hdd_sample_size int 42 Sample size for HD-D (HDD_SAMPLE_SIZE) log_base float 10 Logarithm base for the Summer, Maas and Dugast metrics (DIVERSITY_LOG_BASE)

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
Some metrics depend on conventions that differ between libraries. All of them except the comparison with the MTLD threshold are class parameters:

Parameter Default Other libraries Logarithm base for Summer, Maas, Dugast's U and Dugast's k 10 LexicalRichness, textcomplexity and zipfR - natural MATTR window and MSTTR segment 50 quanteda and koRpus - 100 TTR threshold for MTLD 0.72 0.66-0.75 in the literature Comparison with the MTLD threshold a factor closes at TTR ≤ 0.72 (McCarthy & Jarvis, 2010) lexical-diversity and TAALED - strict <; the values differ when TTR hits the threshold exactly Minimum MTLD factor length 10 koRpus - only in MTLD-MA, dropping shorter factors instead of extending them; LexicalRichness and textcomplexity - not applied HD-D sample size 42 35-50 in the literature

According to Zenker and Kyle (2021), MATTR, MTLD and HD-D are stable on texts of 50-200 words and longer, MTLD-W, MA-MTLD and Maas are unstable on short texts, and the TTR family never stabilizes. Texts of different lengths are compared by the windowed computation with confidence intervals.

docs.title: Type-Token Ratio (TTR)
docs.text:
ttr

calc_ttr(text)

The simplest measure of lexical diversity; it is not corrected for text length.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of lexemes}}{\textrm{Number of words}} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Root Type-Token Ratio (RTTR)
docs.text:
rttr

calc_rttr(text)

A modification of TTR (Guiraud, 1960).

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of lexemes}}{\sqrt{\textrm{(Number of words)}}} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Corrected Type-Token Ratio (CTTR)
docs.text:
cttr

calc_cttr(text)

A modification of TTR (Carroll, 1964).

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of lexemes}}{\sqrt{2\times\textrm{(Number of words)}}} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Herdan Type-Token Ratio (HTTR)
docs.text:
httr

calc_httr(text)

A logarithmic modification of TTR (Herdan, 1960).

\[ \frac{\log_{10} {\textrm{(Number of lexemes)}}}{\log_{10} {{\textrm{(Number of words)}}}} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Summer Type-Token Ratio (STTR)
docs.text:
sttr

calc_sttr(text, base=10)

A logarithmic modification of TTR (Summer, 1966). The value depends on the logarithm base (see the conventions). It is nan for a text of one lexeme, where the numerator is undefined, and for a text no longer than the base (\(\log \log N \le 0\)), including such windows of calc_windowed.

\[ \frac{\log_{10} {\log_{10} {\textrm{(Number of lexemes)}}}}{\log_{10} {\log_{10} {{\textrm{(Number of words)}}}}} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words base float 10 Logarithm base (DIVERSITY_LOG_BASE)

A base that is not a finite number above 1 raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Maas Type-Token Ratio (MTTR)
docs.text:
mttr

calc_mttr(text, base=10)

A logarithmic modification of TTR (Maas, 1972). The value depends on the logarithm base (see the conventions).

\[ \frac{\log_{10} {\textrm{(Number of words)}}-\log_{10} {\textrm{(Number of lexemes)}}}{\log_{10} {{\textrm{(Number of words)}}}^2} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words base float 10 Logarithm base (DIVERSITY_LOG_BASE)

A base that is not a finite number above 1 raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Dugast Type-Token Ratio (DTTR)
docs.text:
dttr

calc_dttr(text, base=10)

A logarithmic modification of TTR (Dugast, 1978), the reciprocal of the Maas metric. The value depends on the logarithm base (see the conventions). A text without repeated words has an infinite value.

\[ \frac{\log_{10} {{\textrm{(Number of words)}}}^2}{\log_{10} {\textrm{(Number of words)}}-\log_{10} {\textrm{(Number of lexemes)}}} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words base float 10 Logarithm base (DIVERSITY_LOG_BASE)

A base that is not a finite number above 1 raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Moving Average Type-Token Ratio (MATTR)
docs.text:
mattr

calc_mattr(text, window_len=50)

A moving-average modification of TTR (Covington & McFall, 2010), independent of text length: a window of fixed size slides over the text, and the TTR of every window is averaged. For texts shorter than the window the TTR of the whole text is returned.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words window_len int 50 Window size (MATTR_WINDOW_LEN)

A window_len that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Mean Segmental Type-Token Ratio (MSTTR)
docs.text:
msttr

calc_msttr(text, segment_len=50)

A segmentation-based modification of TTR (Johnson, 1944), independent of text length: the text is split into segments of fixed size, and the TTR of every segment is averaged; an incomplete last segment is dropped. For texts shorter than the segment the TTR of the whole text is returned.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words segment_len int 50 Segment size (MATTR_WINDOW_LEN)

A segment_len that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Measure of Textual Lexical Diversity (MTLD)
docs.text:
mtld

calc_mtld(text, min_len=10, threshold=0.72)

A modification of MSTTR (McCarthy, 2005), independent of text length: the number of words divided by the number of factors, the stretches on which TTR drops to the threshold (TTR <= threshold, see the conventions). An incomplete last factor counts in proportion to how close its TTR came to the threshold. The value is the mean of a forward and a backward pass (McCarthy & Jarvis, 2010). The minimum factor length is non-standard (Kyle's lexical-diversity), and a min_len of 0 disables it. If no factor completes and TTR never drops below 1, the value is infinity.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words min_len int 10 Minimum factor length (MTLD_MIN_LEN) threshold float 0.72 TTR threshold for completing a factor (MTLD_TTR_THRESHOLD)

A min_len that is not a non-negative integer and a threshold that is not a number in (0, 1) raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Moving Average Measure of Textual Lexical Diversity (MA-MTLD)
docs.text:
mamtld

calc_mamtld(text, min_len=10, threshold=0.72, step=1)

A moving-window modification of MTLD after MTLD-MA of koRpus: a factor starts at every position of the text, and the value is the mean length of the completed factors over a forward and a backward pass. koRpus makes the forward pass only, closes a factor at TTR strictly below the threshold and drops factors shorter than the minimum length instead of extending them. With a step of k a factor starts at every k-th position from either end, as MTLDMA.steps of koRpus. If no factor completes, the value is nan. The metric is unstable on short texts.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words min_len int 10 Minimum factor length (MTLD_MIN_LEN) threshold float 0.72 TTR threshold for completing a factor (MTLD_TTR_THRESHOLD) step int 1 Distance between the starts of the factors

A min_len that is not a non-negative integer, a threshold that is not a number in (0, 1) and a step that is not an integer above 0 raise ParameterError.

docs.title: MTLD with a moving window and text wrap (MTLD-W)
docs.text:
mtldw

calc_mtldw(text, min_len=10, threshold=0.72)

A modification of MA-MTLD after mtld_ma_wrap of lexical-diversity and TAALED: factors not completed by the end of the text continue from its beginning, so all positions get equal weight. A factor cannot be longer than the text. If no factor completes, because the text is shorter than min_len or TTR drops to the threshold from no start, the value is nan. The metric is unstable on texts shorter than 100 words.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words min_len int 10 Minimum factor length (MTLD_MIN_LEN) threshold float 0.72 TTR threshold for completing a factor (MTLD_TTR_THRESHOLD)

A min_len that is not a non-negative integer and a threshold that is not a number in (0, 1) raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Hypergeometric Distribution D (HD-D)
docs.text:
hdd

calc_hdd(text, sample_size=42)

An alternative to vocd-D (McCarthy & Jarvis, 2010): the exact expected TTR of a random sample of sample_size words, without drawing samples. The hypergeometric distribution gives the probability that the sample holds each lexeme at least once; HD-D is the sum of these probabilities divided by the sample size. For texts shorter than 50 words or than the sample size the metric is undefined, and the value is nan.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words sample_size int 42 Sample size in words (HDD_SAMPLE_SIZE)

A sample_size that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Simpson's index (D)
docs.text:
simpson_index · Wikipedia

calc_simpson_index(text)

The probability that two words drawn from the text at random without replacement are the same lexeme; \(n\) is the number of occurrences of a lexeme in the text. For texts shorter than two words the index is undefined, and the value is nan; the same holds for the inverse Simpson's index and the Gini-Simpson index.

\[ \frac{\sum n\times(n-1)}{\textrm{(Number of words)}\times(\textrm{Number of words}-1)} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Inverse Simpson's index (1/D)
docs.text:
inverse_simpson_index · Wikipedia

calc_inverse_simpson_index(text)

An estimate of the Hill number of order two (\(1/\sum_k p_k^2\)) from pairs drawn without replacement. If all words of the text are unique, Simpson's index is 0 and the inverse index is infinity.

\[ \frac{1}{D} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Gini-Simpson index (1-D)
docs.text:
gini_simpson_index · Wikipedia

calc_gini_simpson_index(text)

The probability that two randomly chosen words of the text are different.

\[ 1-D \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Hapax index (Honoré's R)
docs.text:
hapax_index · honore_r · Wikipedia

calc_hapax_index(text)

A hapax (Greek ἅπαξ λεγόμενον - "said only once") is a word that occurs only once in a corpus: baciyelmo, Sancho Panza's word for the barber's basin that Don Quixote takes for a helmet, is a hapax of Cervantes (chapter 44 of the first part of Don Quixote). The index coincides with Honoré's measure (1979), with the natural logarithm. If all words of the text are hapaxes, the index is infinity; for texts shorter than two words it is undefined, and the value is nan. calc_honore_r is the same function.

\[ 100\times\frac{\ln {\textrm{(Number of words)}}}{1-\frac{\textrm{Number of hapaxes}}{\textrm{Number of lexemes}}} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Frequency spectrum
docs.text:
frequency_spectrum

calc_frequency_spectrum(text)

The number of lexemes \(V_i\) occurring exactly \(i\) times in the text, as a dictionary by the frequency \(i\) in ascending order. The hapax index, Yule's K and I, Herdan's Vm, Sichel's S, Michéa's M, Baayen's P, the hapax ratio and the α₂ exponent are computed from it, with the formulas of Tweedie and Baayen (1998).

Notation: \(N\) - number of words, \(V\) - number of lexemes, \(V_i\) - number of lexemes with frequency \(i\), \(V_1\) - hapaxes, \(V_2\) - dis legomena, \(p_k\) - relative frequency of a lexeme.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Yule's characteristic (Yule's K)
docs.text:
yule_k

calc_yule_k(text)

Yule's characteristic (Yule, 1944), one of the few measures theoretically independent of text length (Tweedie & Baayen, 1998); in practice it converges as the text grows. It is proportional to Simpson's index: \(K \approx 10^4 \cdot D\). For texts shorter than two words the value is nan.

\[ K = 10^4\times\frac{\sum_i i^2 V_i - N}{N^2} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Inverse Yule's characteristic (Yule's I)
docs.text:
yule_i

calc_yule_i(text)

The inverse Yule's characteristic. If all words of the text are unique, the value is infinity; for texts shorter than two words it is nan.

\[ I = \frac{V^2}{\sum_i i^2 V_i - V} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Herdan's Vm
docs.text:
herdan_vm

calc_herdan_vm(text)

Herdan's measure (Herdan, 1955), theoretically independent of text length. For texts shorter than two words the value is nan.

\[ V_m = \sqrt{\sum_i V_i \left(\frac{i}{N}\right)^2 - \frac{1}{V}} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Sichel's S
docs.text:
sichel_s

calc_sichel_s(text)

Sichel's measure (Sichel, 1975) - the share of dis legomena, lexemes with frequency 2, among all lexemes. Stable across texts of different lengths.

\[ S = \frac{V_2}{V} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Michéa's M
docs.text:
michea_m

calc_michea_m(text)

Michéa's measure (Michéa, 1969) - the reciprocal of Sichel's measure. If the text has no dis legomena, the value is infinity.

\[ M = \frac{V}{V_2} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Brunet's W
docs.text:
brunet_w

calc_brunet_w(text, a=0.172)

Brunet's measure (Brunet, 1978). Values for texts usually lie within 10-20.

\[ W = N^{V^{-a}}, \quad a = 0.172 \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words a float 0.172 Exponent (BRUNET_W_EXPONENT)

An a that is not a finite number raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Dugast's k
docs.text:
dugast_k

calc_dugast_k(text, base=10)

Dugast's measure (Dugast, 1979), not to be confused with Dugast's U - the DTTR metric. The value depends on the logarithm base. For texts no longer than the base (\(\log N \le 1\)) the measure is undefined, and the value is nan.

\[ k = \frac{\log V}{\log \log N} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words base float 10 Logarithm base (DIVERSITY_LOG_BASE)

A base that is not a finite number above 1 raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Baayen's P
docs.text:
baayen_p

calc_baayen_p(text)

Baayen's measure (Baayen, 1991) - the share of hapaxes among all words of the text. It equals the slope of the vocabulary growth curve at the end of the text: the probability that the next word is new (Evert, 2004).

\[ P = \frac{V_1}{N} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Orlov's Z
docs.text:
orlov_z · Tweedie and Baayen 1998

calc_orlov_z(text)

The text length at which the law of Zipf fits the vocabulary best (Orlov 1983): the solution \(Z\) for \(N\) words, \(V\) lexemes and the share \(p\) of the most frequent lexeme. The right side has a minimum over \(Z\), and \(Z\) is the solution above it; it is nan when \(V\) lies at or below that minimum or when every word is a lexeme of its own, and inf when \(V\) comes so close to \(N\) that \(Z\) overflows a float. With Yule's K, Z separated the authors best among the measures Tweedie and Baayen compared.

\[ V = \frac{Z}{\ln(pZ)} \cdot \frac{N}{N - Z} \cdot \ln \frac{N}{Z} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words CodeResult 
from anyts.diversity_stats import calc_orlov_z

calc_orlov_z("the cat saw the dog and the dog saw a bird near the old tree".split())

59.99999999999961

docs.title: Hapax ratio
docs.text:
hapax_ratio

calc_hapax_ratio(text)

The share of hapaxes among all lexemes of the text.

\[ \frac{V_1}{V} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: The α₂ exponent
docs.text:
alpha2

calc_alpha2(text)

An estimate of the Zipf-Mandelbrot parameter from the lower part of the frequency spectrum (Evert, 2004). If the text has no hapaxes, the value is nan.

\[ \alpha_2 = 1 - \frac{2 V_2}{V_1} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Shannon entropy
docs.text:
entropy · Wikipedia

calc_entropy(text)

The entropy of the lexeme distribution in bits. The Hill number of order one is \(2^H\) (perplexity), of order zero - \(V\); the inverse Simpson's index estimates the one of order two.

\[ H = -\sum_k p_k \log_2 p_k \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Evenness
docs.text:
evenness

calc_evenness(text)

Pielou's evenness - the ratio of the Shannon entropy to its maximum for the given number of lexemes. For texts of a single lexeme it is undefined, and the value is nan.

\[ \frac{H}{\log_2 V} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Perplexity
docs.text:
perplexity

calc_perplexity(text)

The Hill number of order one, the effective number of lexemes of the text.

\[ 2^H \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Zipf's law slope
docs.text:
zipf_alpha · Wikipedia

calc_zipf_alpha(text)

The exponent \(\alpha\) of Zipf's law \(f(r) \propto r^{-\alpha}\), where \(r\) is the frequency rank of a lexeme, estimated by linear regression of log frequency on log rank. For natural texts \(\alpha\) is close to 1. The rank-based least squares estimate is biased; maximum likelihood is more accurate. For texts of a single lexeme the value is nan.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words

docs.title: Zipf-Mandelbrot fit
docs.text:
Wikipedia

fit_zipf_mandelbrot(text)

Fits the Zipf-Mandelbrot law \(f(r) = C / (r + q)^s\) to the rank-frequency distribution. With \(q = 0\) it is Zipf's law with exponent \(s\); the shift \(q\) captures the flattening of the curve on the most frequent words. The fit is by least squares in logarithmic coordinates with \(q \ge 0\), \(s \ge 0\); the lexemes of zero frequency in a counter are left out. The result is a ZipfMandelbrot named tuple with the fields c, q, s and r2 - the coefficient of determination of the fit in logarithmic coordinates. All fields are nan for texts of fewer than three lexemes, with identical frequencies of all lexemes or when the fit diverges. The parameters are unstable on short texts: the law describes large corpora.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] / Counter - List of words or a counter of their frequencies

A counter whose words are not strings or whose frequencies are not numbers raises SourceTypeError, and a negative, nan or infinite frequency SourceError (check_counts).

CodeResult 
from anyts.diversity_stats import fit_zipf_mandelbrot

# the frequencies 12, 6, 4, 3 follow the law f = 12 / r exactly
words = ["a"] * 12 + ["b"] * 6 + ["c"] * 4 + ["d"] * 3
fit = fit_zipf_mandelbrot(words)
round(fit.c, 3), round(fit.q, 3), round(fit.s, 3), round(fit.r2, 3)

(12.001, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0)

docs.title: Heaps' law exponent
docs.text:
heaps_beta · Wikipedia

calc_heaps_beta(text)

The exponent \(\beta\) of Heaps' law \(V(N) = K \cdot N^{\beta}\) of vocabulary growth with text length, estimated by linear regression of log vocabulary size on log text length along the growth curve. On corpora of millions of words \(\beta\) lies within 0.4-0.6, on a single text within 0.6-0.9, so the values are comparable only between texts of similar length. The value depends on word order and needs several hundred words or more. For texts shorter than two words the value is nan.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words 
vocabulary_growth(text)

The vocabulary growth curve of a list of words: the vocabulary size after every word of the text.

fit_heaps(text)

Fits Heaps' law over the vocabulary growth curve of a list of words, as calc_heaps_beta does, and returns a HeapsFit named tuple with the parameters k, beta and the coefficient of determination r2, all nan for texts shorter than two words; r2 is nan for a text of one lexeme too.

docs.title: Burstiness
docs.text:
burstiness · Kim and Jo 2016

calc_burstiness(text, min_freq=5)

How a lexeme comes in bursts rather than spread over the text, by the burstiness of Kim and Jo, which corrects that of Goh and Barabási for a finite number \(n\) of events, averaged over the lexemes of min_freq occurrences or more (BURSTINESS_MIN_FREQ). For the \(n\) occurrences of a lexeme, \(r\) is the coefficient of variation of their \(n\) intervals, the one from the last to the first around the end of the text included. The value is −1 for occurrences at equal intervals, near 0 for a rare lexeme at random places and up to 1 for occurrences in bursts; nan without such lexemes.

\[ A_n = \frac{\sqrt{n + 1} \cdot r - \sqrt{n - 1}}{(\sqrt{n + 1} - 2) \cdot r + \sqrt{n - 1}} \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words min_freq int 5 Smallest number of occurrences of a lexeme measured

A min_freq that is not an integer of at least 2 raises ParameterError.

CodeResult 
from anyts.diversity_stats import calc_burstiness

calc_burstiness("a x a x a x a x a x".split()), calc_burstiness("a a a a a x x x x x".split())

(-1.0, 0.18350341907227388)

docs.title: Windowed computation
docs.text:
windowed(stat)

calc_windowed(text, func, window_len=100, step=None, confidence=0.95, *, messages=MESSAGES)

The values of a metric over consecutive windows of equal length give their mean, their sample standard deviation and the confidence interval of the mean by Student's distribution. The standard way to compare texts of different lengths; Kubát and Milička's standardized TTR (not Summer's STTR) is a windowed TTR with a 1000-word window and a 95% interval. A text shorter than the window is a single window; nan windows are ignored. With fewer than two windows of a defined value the deviation and the interval are nan, and without any the mean too. A metric infinite in any window (e.g. the inverse Simpson's index on a window of unique words) makes the mean infinite and the deviation and the interval nan. The result is a WindowStats named tuple with the fields mean, std, lower, upper and n_windows, the number of the windows of a defined value.

Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words func Callable - Function computing the metric from a list of words window_len int 100 Window size step int None Window step; the window size by default, so the windows do not overlap confidence float 0.95 Confidence level messages dict[str, str] MESSAGES Messages of the errors by key

A func that cannot be called raises SourceTypeError; a window_len or a step that is not an integer of at least one and a confidence that is not a number in (0, 1) raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Lexical sophistication
docs.text:
LexicalStats(source, freq_dict=None)

Lexical sophistication in the manner of TAALES (Kyle, Crossley and Berger, 2018) - how rare the words of a text are: statistics by a frequency dictionary and its unigram model, the shares of the frequency bands of a list of the most frequent lemmas and the lexical density. The statistics by the dictionary are computed when first read, so the bands and the lexical density need no dictionary data.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a dictionary of another class than that of the library or, without freq_dict_class, one without lookup and ipm or none at all; an analyze that does not give LexicalWord objects;
  • SourceError - a source without words.
CodeResult 
from typing import NamedTuple

from anyts.lexical_stats import LexicalStats, LexicalWord


class Entry(NamedTuple):
    ipm: float
    range: int
    dispersion: float


class Frequencies:
    min_ipm = 0.5
    entries = {"the": Entry(50000.0, 40, 0.99), "cat": Entry(100.0, 38, 0.9)}

    def lookup(self, lemma):
        return self.entries.get(lemma)

    def ipm(self, lemma):
        entry = self.lookup(lemma)
        return entry.ipm if entry is not None else 0.0


class Lexical(LexicalStats):
    freq_dict_class = Frequencies

    def analyze(self, source):
        return [LexicalWord(word, word.lower(), word.lower() != "the") for word in source.split()]

    def rank(self, lemma):
        return {"the": 1, "cat": 1500}.get(lemma)


stats = Lexical("The cat sees the dog")
stats.print_stats()

docs.title: Frequency dictionary
docs.text:
The dictionary is any object of the protocol FrequencyDictionary: lookup(lemma) gives the entry of a lemma or None, ipm(lemma) its frequency per million words or 0, and min_ipm the lowest frequency of the dictionary, above zero. An entry (FrequencyEntry) has the frequency ipm, above zero, the range range (the parts of the corpus with the lemma) and the dispersion dispersion. Without freq_dict_class a dictionary without lookup and ipm raises SourceTypeError.

FrequencyEntry is the entry of a lemma in a FrequencyDictionary: ipm, range and dispersion.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Every metric is an attribute or a property of the object, and get_stats gives them all. A mean is over the words found in the dictionary, and without them it is nan.

Metric Measures Range Higher means coverage Share of the words found in the dictionary 0-1 More words known to the dictionary mean_ipm, mean_ipm_content Mean frequency per million words of the words found, of the content words found Above 0 More frequent words mean_log_ipm, mean_log_ipm_content Mean decimal logarithm of the frequency of the words found, of the content words found Up to 6 More frequent words mean_range Mean range of the words found 0 and above Words used in more parts of the corpus mean_dispersion Mean dispersion of the words found That of the dictionary By the measure of the dictionary surprisal Mean surprisal of the words by the unigram model of the dictionary, in bits 0 and above Rarer words perplexity 2 to the power of the surprisal 1 and above Rarer words p_top1000, p_top2000, p_top5000, p_top10000 Share of the words with a lemma in the top 1000, 2000, 5000 and 10000 of the list 0-1, nan for a band beyond top_size More frequent words p_beyond_top10000 Share of the words with a lemma beyond the top 10000 0-1, nan for a list shorter than 10000 Rarer words lexical_density Share of the content words 0-1 More content words

docs.title: Surprisal and perplexity
docs.text:
surprisal · perplexity

calc_surprisal(lemmas, freq_dict)

The mean surprisal of the words by the unigram model of a frequency dictionary, in bits; a word out of the dictionary gets its lowest frequency min_ipm. The perplexity is 2 to its power.

\[ \frac{1}{N} \sum_{w} -\log_2 \frac{\max(\textrm{ipm}_w, \textrm{min\_ipm})}{10^6} \] Parameter Type Default Description lemmas list[str] - Keys of the words in the dictionary freq_dict FrequencyDictionary - Frequency dictionary

No words give nan; keys that are not a list of strings and a dictionary without ipm and min_ipm raise SourceTypeError, a lowest frequency that is not above zero ParameterError.

docs.title: Frequency bands
docs.text:
p_top1000 · p_top2000 · p_top5000 · p_top10000 · p_beyond_top10000 · band_coverage(bands, unique)

The share of the words whose lemma has a rank (rank) within the top \(N\) of the list, for the bounds 1000, 2000, 5000 and 10000 of FREQUENCY_BANDS; the share beyond the top 10000 is the rest, the words out of the list included. A band beyond the size of the list (top_size) is nan, and so is the share beyond the top 10000 for a list shorter than 10000.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of words with a rank up to } N}{\textrm{Number of words}} \]

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
band_coverage(bands, unique) gives the share of the words with a lemma in the top N of the list for every bound N of bands (FREQUENCY_BANDS by default), or with unique=True the share of the distinct lemmas. Bounds that are not a list of integers or a bound out of 1 and top_size() raise ParameterError.

stats.band_coverage([1000, 2000], unique=True)

{1000: 0.4, 2000: 0.6}

docs.title: Morphological statistics
docs.text:
MorphStats(source)

The morphological statistics of a text: the part of speech and the features of Universal Dependencies of every word, counted by value or given word by word. By default the data source is a Doc object of spaCy with the parts of speech, read by token.pos_ and token.morph; a language library reads a string or a Doc without them in its own way.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is not a Doc, an analyze that does not give MorphWord objects;

PhonStats(source, words_extractor=None, window_len=3)

The phonetic statistics of a text: its sounds by class, their clusters, sequences and repetitions, and its syllables. A sound is a letter of a word by default, or a sound of its transcription when a library gives one. The data source is a text or a Doc object of spaCy; the words are taken in lower case, and an extractor passed explicitly is used on the text of a Doc.

import re

from anyts.phon_stats import PhonStats

docs.title: Alliteration and assonance
docs.text:
alliteration · assonance

calc_repetition_index(words, window_len, features=None)

The repetition index: the number of windows of window_len neighbouring words where a feature (a letter or a sound) occurs in two words or more, summed over the features, divided by the number expected if the words stood in random order. A window of shuffled words is a sample without replacement, so for a feature found in \(K\) of the \(N\) words, a window of \(w\) words holds it in two words or more with the hypergeometric probability

\[ P = 1 - \frac{\binom{N-K}{w} + K \binom{N-K}{w-1}}{\binom{N}{w}} \]

and the expected number is the sum of these probabilities over the features times the \(N - w + 1\) windows. Since the expectation comes from the text itself, the index shows whether the repetitions gather in neighbouring words, not how frequent a feature is: it averages to 1 over the orders of the words and is well above 1 when the repetitions come closer than chance. A word counts a feature once; the index is nan for a text shorter than the window or with no feature shared by two words.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] / list[list[str]] - Features of every word: a string of its letters or a collection of its sounds window_len int - Window in words, at least 2 features Collection[str] None Features to count, all of them by default

Words that are not a list of strings or of collections of strings and features that are not a collection of strings raise SourceTypeError, and a window_len that is not an integer of at least 2 ParameterError.

p_open_syllables · mean_syllable_len

The syllables are the sounds of every syllable of a word by syllable_sounds; a syllable without a sound of the classes (a number) is no syllable, in c_syllable_patterns too. An open syllable ends in a vowel by its CV pattern (cv_pattern), and the length of a syllable is the length of that pattern: the sounds of the classes, without skipped and the signs out of them.

docs.title: Readability metrics
docs.text:
ReadabilityStats(source, sents_extractor=None, words_extractor=None, preset='original')

The readability metrics of a text from its basic statistics: the mean sentence length in words, the mean word length in syllables or letters, the share of polysyllabic and of long words and the variability of word length. The data source is a text, a Doc object of spaCy or ready basic statistics, which are reused as they are; the extractors are passed on to the basic statistics of a text or a Doc. The formulas count only the letters of the counted words, so a word extractor that drops words does not lengthen the mean word.

The metrics are properties computed on each access, so a change of the coefficients of an object applies at once.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is neither a string, a Doc nor basic statistics, basic statistics of a class other than those of the library, an extractor of another type, a string or a Doc to a class without basic_stats_class;
  • SourceError - a source without words or sentences;
  • ParameterError - an unknown preset or one that is not a string.

A subclass with the basic statistics of a language - here the syllables are the groups of vowels, a rough rule for English.

import re

from anyts.basic_stats import BasicStats
from anyts.readability_stats import ReadabilityStats


class Stats(BasicStats):
    def count_syllables(self, word):
        return len(re.findall(r"[aeiouy]+", word, re.IGNORECASE))


class Readability(ReadabilityStats):
    basic_stats_class = Stats


rs = Readability("The cat sat on the mat. A beautiful day!")
rs.print_stats()

consensus_grade

The consensus_grade attribute is the median of the values of the grade formulas (grade_stats) rounded half up, together with the reading ease in years of schooling (reading_ease_to_grade), not rounded. A library aligns the bounds of reading_ease_grades, and of each scale of preset_reading_ease_grades, with its scale of the reading ease, so that the consensus grade and describe read the value alike.

calc_consensus_grade(grades, flesch_reading_easy=None, to_grade=flesch_reading_easy_to_grade)

The median of the values of the grade formulas rounded half up, together with the reading ease in years of schooling by to_grade, not rounded - so a band of 8.5 votes for 8.5.

\[ \textrm{median}\left(\lfloor g_1 + 0.5 \rfloor, \ldots, \lfloor g_k + 0.5 \rfloor, \textrm{to\_grade}(\textrm{reading ease})\right) \] Parameter Type Default Description grades list[float] - Values of the grade formulas flesch_reading_easy float None Value of the reading ease to_grade Callable flesch_reading_easy_to_grade Conversion of the reading ease into years of schooling

Conversion of the Flesch reading ease into years of schooling for the consensus grade: the grade of the first band whose lower bound the value reaches, or below under the last bound; values above 100 belong to the first band. A reading ease or a below that is not a finite number raises ParameterError, and so do grades that are empty or not pairs of finite numbers with descending bounds.

The default bands are those of text_standard of textstat, which follow the table of Flesch (1948) down to 60 and split his lower bands, with 8.5 for its grades 8 and 9: 90-100 - 5, 80-90 - 6, 70-80 - 7, 60-70 - 8.5, 50-60 - 10, 40-50 - 11, 30-40 - 12, below 30 - 13 (anyts.constants.READING_EASE_GRADES).

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
describe_grade(stat) returns the school stage and reader age for the consensus grade or the grade formula stat, consensus_grade by default; another metric raises ParameterError.

describe_level(stat) returns the band of the interpretation scale (level_scale) of the metric stat, flesch_reading_easy by default; a metric without a scale of bands and an undefined value (nan) raise ParameterError.

describe(stat) returns the reading of any metric by its scale: for the consensus grade and a grade formula the school stage and reader age (describe_grade), for a metric with a scale of bands (level_scale) its band, for another metric of grade_scales the stage and age of the years of schooling its scale gives, and None for a metric without a scale or with an undefined value (nan). A name that is neither in stats_desc nor a public property of the class raises UnknownStatError.

reading_time_by_speed(wpm) returns the reading time of the text in minutes at the speed wpm, words per minute; a speed that is not a positive number raises ParameterError.

reading_time_by_norm(norm) returns the reading times of the text in minutes at the speeds of the norm norm of reading_speed_norms, in their order; an unknown norm raises ParameterError.

get_stats() returns a dictionary of the readability metrics of stats_desc.

print_stats() prints a table of the readability metrics with their descriptions from stats_desc under the headers of stats_headers.

from anyts.stats import Stats


class TextSize(Stats):
    stats_desc = {"n_words": "Words", "c_lengths": "Words by length"}
    level_scales = {"n_words": ((100, "long"), (0, "short"))}

    def __init__(self, text):
        words = text.split()
        self.n_words = len(words)
        self.c_lengths = {3: sum(len(word) == 3 for word in words)}


size = TextSize("The cat sat on the mat")
size.print_stats()

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
get_stats(flat=False) returns a copy of the statistics of stat_names: editing it does not change the object. With flat=True the values of a dictionary statistic become keys of their own, joined to its name with an underscore: the distribution {3: 5} of c_lengths gives the key c_lengths_3.

to_dataframe() returns the flat statistics, get_stats(flat=True), as a one-row DataFrame of pandas with a column for every key. A dictionary statistic gives columns only for the keys the text has, so in frames of several texts joined with pandas.concat a count a text lacks is NaN. Only these columns may be filled with 0: elsewhere NaN is an undefined value.

print_stats() prints a table of the statistics of stats_desc with their descriptions under the headers of stats_headers, floats with two decimals; each column is as wide as its longest text.

describe(stat) returns the band of the scale of the statistic stat (level_scale), and None for a statistic without a scale, with an undefined value (nan) or for a key of the flat statistics (get_stats(flat=True)), a key of any value of a dictionary statistic included, as the table of another text may have it. A name that is neither of stat_names nor a public property of the class raises UnknownStatError.

size.describe("n_words")

StyleStats(source, words_extractor=None, stopwords=None, top_n=10, cliches=None, nausea_stopwords=None)

The style metrics of a text: the SEO metrics of Advego and Text.ru and the markers of the officialese style. The services publish no formulas, so the common definitions are taken. The data source is a text or a Doc object of spaCy.

The SEO metrics are counted on the words of the word extractor, in lower case by default, or on the tokens of a Doc; an extractor passed explicitly is used on the text of a Doc. The markers are counted on the word forms in lower case (forms), whatever the extractor.

docs.title: Naturalness by Zipf's law
docs.text:
zipf_naturalness

calc_zipf_naturalness(text, top_n=10, *, messages=MESSAGES)

The agreement of the frequencies of the most frequent words with the ideal distribution \(f_r = f_1 / r\), where \(r\) is the rank. The first rank is ideal by construction, and above \(f_1\) the ideal frequency falls below one, so the ranks run from 2 to \(R = \min(\textrm{top\_n}, V, f_1)\). Negative values are cut to 0. Without ranks to compare - all the words hapaxes, one lexeme or top_n below 2 - the value is nan.

\[ 100 \cdot \left(1 - \frac{1}{R - 1} \sum_{r=2}^{R} \frac{|r \cdot f_r - f_1|}{f_1}\right) \] Parameter Type Default Description text list[str] - List of words top_n int 10 Number of the most frequent words (NAUSEA_TOP_N) messages dict[str, str] MESSAGES Messages of the errors by key

docs.text:
leaves_per_sent · subtrees_per_sent · nodes_per_leaf

A leaf is a word without dependent words (count_children), a subtree a word with them. The nodes per leaf are the words of a sentence over its leaves, averaged over the \(S\) sentences.

\[ \frac{1}{S} \sum_{s=1}^{S} \frac{\textrm{Number of words of } s}{\textrm{Number of leaves of } s} \]

docs.title: Words before the root
docs.text:
words_before_root · Coh-Metrix

The left embeddedness of Coh-Metrix (SYNLE): the number of the words of a sentence before its root, the main predicate, averaged over the sentences whose root is a word. The root of a sentence with a copula is its nominal part (she is a doctor**), as Universal Dependencies has it. In a language with a free word order the measure reads the order as much as the complexity.

docs.title: Valency of the finite verbs
docs.text:
verb_valency

calc_valency(token, join_hyphens=False)

The valency of a token: the number of its dependent words, the relations cc, conj, parataxis and punct left out (anyts.constants.VALENCY_IGNORED_DEPS); with join_hyphens=True a hyphenated dependent counts once, so came in Some-one came has one dependent and not two.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

docs.title: Coordination chains
docs.text:
coordination_chains_per_sent · mean_coordination_chain_len

calc_coordination_chains(tokens, join_hyphens=False)

The lengths of the coordination chains, in the order of their first words. A chain is a group of words linked by conj, whichever word each conjunct hangs on: Universal Dependencies attaches every conjunct to the first one (pears → apples, plums → apples), ClearNLP to the previous one (pears → apples, plums → pears); both give one chain of three for apples, pears and plums. A nested coordination (cats and dogs, or birds) and an enumeration split between several heads are one chain too. The length of a chain is the number of its words; a conjunct whose head lies outside the sequence is not linked to it. With join_hyphens a hyphenated word is one conjunct, linked by the conj of any of its parts (member and vice-governor is a chain of two).

Parameter Type Default Description tokens Doc / Span / list[Token] - Sequence of tokens join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

docs.title: Clauses
docs.text:
clauses_per_sent · mean_clause_len

is_clause_head(token, join_hyphens=False, is_infinitive_periphrasis=None, auxiliary_form=None)

Checks whether a word heads a clause: the head of the sentence or a word with ccomp, advcl, acl, csubj or parataxis (anyts.constants.CLAUSE_DEPS, subtypes included) whose predicate (predicate_form, so has been built is finite) is not a participle, a converb or a gerund (NONFINITE_CLAUSE_FORMS, counted apart), nor an infinitive under acl; under xcomp, a finite predicate or an infinitive clause (is_infinitive_clause). A parataxis and a conjunct of a clause head count only as predicates (is_predicate); an infinitive conjunct and an infinitive subject (csubj) are no clause by the check is_infinitive_periphrasis, since a model may attach the infinitive of a periphrasis to its verb as conj and to a modal word as csubj; a loop of conjuncts is no clause.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word is_infinitive_periphrasis Callable[[Token], bool] None Whether an infinitive makes one predicate with its head; none by default auxiliary_form Callable[[Token], str] None Verb form of an auxiliary without VerbForm (predicate_form); none by default

A value that is not a Token and a check of a periphrasis or a form of an auxiliary that is not callable raise SourceTypeError.

is_infinitive_clause(token, is_infinitive_periphrasis=None, is_clause_head=None, auxiliary_form=None)

Checks whether an infinitive complement heads a clause of its own: an infinitive (predicate_form, so to be chosen is one) under xcomp (wants to leave), unless the language check is_infinitive_periphrasis says it makes one predicate with its head (can leave, begins to leave), or the word it completes, the first one up its chain of non-finite complements under xcomp (kept trying to leave, seemed able to leave) and of the infinitives of a periphrasis that a model attaches as conj or csubj, heads no clause by the check is_clause_head: an infinitive in a participial phrase or under an infinitive under acl (trying to leave, the wish to try to leave) belongs to that phrase. A ClearNLP parse hangs an infinitive after a predicative adjective on an acomp or oprd (is ready to leave), which heads no clause, so that infinitive is none.

docs.title: Production units of L2SCA
docs.text:
t_units_per_sent · mean_t_unit_len · clauses_per_t_unit · p_complex_t_units · verb_phrases_per_t_unit · coordinate_phrases_per_clause · complex_nominals_per_clause · Lu 2010

The indices of the L2 Syntactic Complexity Analyzer (L2SCA) that the other metrics do not give, on Universal Dependencies. MLC and C/S are mean_clause_len and clauses_per_sent; MLS and DC/C come from the counts, n_words / n_sents and n_subordinate_clauses / n_clauses.

  • A T-unit is a main clause with the clauses that depend on it: the head of a sentence and every clause head joined to it through conj or parataxis (anyts.constants.MAIN_CLAUSE_DEPS), so I came, and he left holds two; a conjunct of a subordinate clause is none. A T-unit is complex with a subordinate clause (is_subordinate_clause_head) whose nearest T-unit above is it.
  • A verb phrase is a predicate (is_predicate) that is no auxiliary or copula: a verb, an auxiliary used as a predicate (there is trouble), a word with a subject or a copula.
  • A coordinate phrase is a coordination with a conjunct that is no clause head (the man and the woman, is big and nice), counted once by its first conjunct; a coordination of clause heads counts as clauses.
  • A complex nominal is a noun with a modifier of anyts.constants.COMPLEX_NOMINAL_DEPS (an adjective, a complement, a relative or participial clause, an apposition, a possessive), or a nominal clause, a clause head of anyts.constants.NOMINAL_CLAUSE_DEPS or a conjunct of one.
\[ \textrm{MLT} = \frac{\textrm{Words}}{\textrm{T-units}}, \quad \textrm{C/T} = \frac{\textrm{Clauses}}{\textrm{T-units}}, \quad \textrm{CT/T} = \frac{\textrm{Complex T-units}}{\textrm{T-units}}, \quad \textrm{CN/C} = \frac{\textrm{Complex nominals}}{\textrm{Clauses}} \]

docs.text:
modifiers_per_noun

count_noun_modifiers(token, join_hyphens=False)

Counts the modifiers of a noun phrase: the dependents with the relations amod, det, nmod, nummod, acl and their subtypes (anyts.constants.NOUN_MODIFIER_DEPS); conj and appos are no modifiers.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

docs.title: Prepositional chains
docs.text:
prep_chains_per_sent · max_prep_chain_len · Profiling-UD

A prepositional chain is two or more nested complements with a preposition, each hanging on the previous one: on the mat of the house of the mayor (length 3). The links are the words of the hook is_prep_complement, and the chains and their lengths are those of calc_modifier_chains; a chain may start at a complement of a verb (obl) or at a prepositional predicate with a copula (was in the house of the mayor), but not at a conjunct of a complement (in Madrid and in the centre of the city), and a predicate of a relative clause (the house that was by the river) is no link of the chain of its noun. The chains read Universal Dependencies alone: ClearNLP heads a phrase by its preposition (prep, pobj), so its parses give no chains.

is_prep_complement(token, join_hyphens=False)

Checks whether a word is a complement with a preposition: a word with the relation nmod or obl or a subtype of them (anyts.constants.PREP_COMPLEMENT_DEPS), or a predicate with a copula out of a relative clause (acl), that has a dependent of the relation case that is an adposition (ADP) or begins one of several words (fixed: in front of). A noun in a case without a preposition and a possessive marker are none.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

A value that is not a Token raises SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Participial clauses
docs.text:
participle_clauses_per_sent · mean_participle_clause_len

The clauses headed by the words of the hook is_participle_clause; the length of a clause is the number of the words in the subtree of its head (subtree_len).

docs.title: Passive
docs.text:
p_passive · p_agentless_passive

is_passive(token, join_hyphens=False)

Checks whether a word is a passive verb form: a verb with Voice=Pass or a dependent nsubj:pass, csubj:pass, aux:pass, or nsubjpass, csubjpass, auxpass of ClearNLP (PASSIVE_DEPS).

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

A value that is not a Token raises SourceTypeError.

has_agent(token, join_hyphens=False)

Checks whether a word has an agent: a dependent obl:agent, or agent of ClearNLP (AGENT_DEPS). The arguments and the error are those of is_passive.

is_agentless(token, join_hyphens=False)

Checks whether a word is a passive form (is_passive) without an agent (has_agent), with the same arguments and error.

docs.title: Infinitives, negations and split predicates
docs.text:
infinitives_per_sent · negations_per_sent · split_predicates_per_sent

The infinitives (is_infinitive of anyts.utils), the words of negation of the hook is_negation and the split predicates of the hook find_split_predicates, per sentence.

docs.title: Order of the subjects and the objects
docs.text:
p_preverbal_subjects · p_preverbal_objects · Profiling-UD

The order of the subjects and of the direct objects in the manner of Profiling-UD: the shares of those before their head, the predicate. Only the nominal ones (NOUN, PROPN) count: the place of a pronoun, such as a clitic object, is set by the grammar. A subject is a word of nsubj (anyts.constants.NOMINAL_SUBJECT_DEPS), an object one of obj (anyts.constants.OBJECT_DEPS), with the relations of ClearNLP and the subtypes.

\[ \frac{\textrm{Nominal subjects before their head}}{\textrm{Nominal subjects}}, \quad \frac{\textrm{Nominal objects before their head}}{\textrm{Nominal objects}} \]

docs.title: Similarity of adjacent sentences
docs.text:
pos_edit_distance · syntax_similarity · Coh-Metrix

How alike the structures of two adjacent sentences are, averaged over the \(S - 1\) pairs. pos_edit_distance is the edit distance of the parts of speech \(P_s\) of the words of the sentences (SYNMEDpos of Coh-Metrix) over the length \(n\) of the longer sentence of the pair, calc_edit_distance. syntax_similarity is the similarity of the multisets of the dependency triples \(T\) of the two sentences (dependency_triples, calc_multiset_similarity), in the manner of SYNSTRUT of Coh-Metrix, which compares the nodes of phrase-structure trees. Both are nan for a Doc without parts of speech.

\[ \frac{1}{S - 1} \sum_{s=1}^{S-1} \frac{\textrm{lev}(P_s, P_{s+1})}{\max(n_s, n_{s+1})}, \quad \frac{1}{S - 1} \sum_{s=1}^{S-1} \frac{|T_s \cap T_{s+1}|}{|T_s \cup T_{s+1}|} \] 
dependency_triples(tokens, join_hyphens=False)

The dependency triples of the words of a sentence (get_words), in their order: the part of speech of the head of a word - the nearest word above it through punctuation - its relation without a subtype (base_dep) and its own part of speech, such as ("NOUN", "amod", "ADJ") for a red house. The head of the sentence, and a word with no word above it, give an empty head and the relation root, whatever its label.

Parameter Type Default Description tokens Doc / Span / list[Token] - Sequence of tokens join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word 
calc_edit_distance(sents)

The mean edit distance of the items of adjacent sentences: the Levenshtein distance of every two - the fewest insertions, deletions and substitutions that turn one into the other - over the number of the items of the longer one, 0 for the same sequences and 1 for ones with no item in common; nan for fewer than two sentences.

Parameter Type Default Description sents list[list] - Items of every sentence, such as its parts of speech

Sentences that are not a list of lists raise SourceTypeError.

calc_multiset_similarity(sents)

The mean similarity of the multisets of the items of adjacent sentences: the weighted Jaccard similarity of every two - the items they share, each as many times as the sentence with fewer of them has it, over the items of both, each as many times as the sentence with more of them has it - 1 for the same multisets and for two empty ones, 0 for disjoint ones; nan for fewer than two sentences. A mapping is read by its keys, as a set.

Parameter Type Default Description sents list[list] - Items of every sentence, such as its dependency triples

Sentences that are not a list of collections raise SourceTypeError.

CodeResult 
from anyts.syntax_stats import calc_edit_distance, calc_multiset_similarity

calc_edit_distance([["DET", "NOUN", "VERB"], ["DET", "ADJ", "NOUN", "VERB"]])
calc_multiset_similarity([["a", "a", "b"], ["a", "b", "b"]])

0.25
0.5

noun_verb_ratio
