\[ \frac{\textrm{Number of nouns}}{\textrm{Number of verb forms}} \]

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
The methods get_stats, to_dataframe, print_stats and describe are those of the statistics interface.

The functions of the tree take a spaCy Doc, a Span or a list of tokens; its words are the tokens of anyts.utils.is_word. They read the relations that Universal Dependencies and the ClearNLP labels of the English models share: the head of a token, cc, conj, parataxis, punct and aux, the subjects nsubj and csubj, the modifiers of a noun amod, det, nmod, nummod and acl, the clause relations ccomp, advcl and xcomp, and the root; the copula cop of predicate_form and is_predicate exists in Universal Dependencies alone. The passive and its agent (is_passive, has_agent) and the order of the subjects and the objects read the relations of both schemes (PASSIVE_DEPS, AGENT_DEPS, NOMINAL_SUBJECT_DEPS, OBJECT_DEPS); the prepositional complements of is_prep_complement read Universal Dependencies alone. Everything else is up to a language library.

docs.title: Words of a sequence
docs.text:
get_words(tokens, join_hyphens=False)

The words of a sequence of tokens in their order; with join_hyphens=True a word the tokenizer split at its hyphens is one word, given by its part that holds its relation, as with the dependents of get_children (governor in He is vice-governor), or by its first part when a hyphen holds it.

Parameter Type Default Description tokens Doc / Span / list[Token] - Sequence of tokens join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

docs.title: Hyphenated words
docs.text: A tokenizer may split a word at its hyphens (well-known into well, -, known), and a parser then hangs every part on its own head. With join_hyphens=True the functions of the tree take a word whose parts anyts.utils.joins_previous joins for one word with its hyphens. A word holding the head of the sentence has no head; the head of another one is that of its part hanging outside it, the nearest to the root (a word rather than a hyphen when equal). The dependents of a word are the words whose head hangs on one of its tokens, each given by that part (or by its first part when it hangs by a hyphen); its subtree is the word and the words that hang on it, directly or through punctuation. So every word has one dependency and is the dependent of one word.

docs.title: Head of a sentence
docs.text:
is_root(token)

Checks whether a token is the head of its sentence: its head is the token itself.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token

docs.title: Base relation
docs.text:
base_dep(token)

The relation of a token without its subtype, which Universal Dependencies separates by a colon: nsubj:pass gives nsubj, expl:pass gives expl.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token

docs.title: Dependent words
docs.text:
get_children(token, join_hyphens=False)

The dependent words of a token, punctuation and whitespace left out; with join_hyphens=True, the dependents of the whole hyphenated word the token belongs to.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word 
count_children(token, join_hyphens=False)

The number of the dependent words of a token; the arguments are those of get_children.

subtree_len(token, join_hyphens=False)

The number of words in the subtree of a token: the token itself and all of its direct and indirect dependents; the arguments are those of get_children.

docs.title: Verb form of a predicate
docs.text:
predicate_form(token, auxiliary_form=None)

The verb form of a predicate by the forms (VerbForm) of its auxiliaries and copulas (aux and cop with their subtypes, anyts.constants.AUXILIARY_DEPS), as Universal Dependencies annotates them. A finite auxiliary makes the predicate finite wherever it stands (had arrived, the German gekommen sein wird); otherwise the first auxiliary decides (to have gone is an infinitive, being chosen a gerund), and without auxiliaries the word itself. A past participle auxiliary counts as finite, since it follows a finite one the parser may attach to another word (had been chosen); a present participle (having eaten) does not. A ClearNLP parse has no copula relation: its copula heads the clause with its own form, and its passive auxiliary auxpass is not read. An auxiliary the model leaves without a form is read by the language hook auxiliary_form, which gives its form or an empty string to skip it; without the hook it is skipped. A word with no verb form gives an empty string.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token auxiliary_form Callable[[Token], str] None Verb form of an auxiliary without VerbForm

A value that is not a Token and a hook that is not callable raise SourceTypeError.

CodeResult 
import spacy
from spacy.tokens import Doc

from anyts.syntax_stats import predicate_form

vocab = spacy.blank("en").vocab
doc = Doc(
    vocab,
    words=["She", "had", "been", "chosen"],
    heads=[3, 3, 3, 3],
    deps=["nsubj:pass", "aux", "aux:pass", "ROOT"],
    morphs=["Case=Nom", "VerbForm=Fin", "VerbForm=Part", "VerbForm=Part"],
)
predicate_form(doc[3])
# An auxiliary the model left without a form, read by the hook
doc = Doc(
    vocab,
    words=["to", "have", "gone"],
    heads=[2, 2, 2],
    deps=["mark", "aux", "ROOT"],
    morphs=["", "", "VerbForm=Part"],
)
predicate_form(doc[2]), predicate_form(doc[2], lambda aux: "Inf" if aux.lower_ == "have" else "")

docs.text:
is_predicate(token, join_hyphens=False)

Checks whether a word can be the predicate of its clause: a verb (VERB, AUX), a word with a subject of its own (nsubj, csubj and their subtypes, anyts.constants.SUBJECT_DEPS) or with a copula (cop), so the nominal predicate of he is tall and of a language that drops the subject passes and a parenthetical word does not.

docs.title: Chains of modifiers
docs.text:
calc_modifier_chains(tokens, is_modifier, join_hyphens=False)

The lengths of the chains of nested modifiers, in the order of the words. A chain is two or more modifiers each hanging on the previous one, such as the complements of the increase of the efficiency of the use of resources (length 3); the check is_modifier of a language says what a modifier is (a complement with a preposition, a noun in the genitive). A chain starts at a modifier whose head is none, and its length is the number of modifiers in its longest branch. The links are those of get_children: punctuation is no link, and with join_hyphens a hyphenated word is one link.

Parameter Type Default Description tokens Doc / Span / list[Token] - Sequence of tokens is_modifier Callable[[Token], bool] - Whether a word is a modifier of the chain join_hyphens bool False Take a hyphenated word for one word

A check that is not callable raises SourceTypeError.

from spacy.tokens import Doc

from anyts.syntax_stats import calc_modifier_chains

    words=["the", "use", "of", "the", "water", "of", "the", "river"],
    heads=[1, 1, 4, 4, 1, 7, 7, 4],
    deps=["det", "ROOT", "case", "det", "nmod", "case", "det", "nmod"],

docs.title: For library developers
docs.text:
Language hooks of a subclass

A language library subclasses SyntaxStats. The defaults read Universal Dependencies with its morphological features and the relations it shares with ClearNLP; the passive, its agent and the order of the subjects and the objects read the relations of both, the prepositional chains those of Universal Dependencies:

Hook Kind Description parse(source) method Doc of a source; by default the source itself, which must be a Doc; a library may parse a string is_clause_head(token) method Whether a word heads a clause; by default is_clause_head of the module with join_hyphens of the class and the hooks is_infinitive_periphrasis and auxiliary_form is_infinitive_periphrasis(token) method Whether an infinitive under xcomp, an infinitive conjunct or an infinitive subject (csubj) of a modal word makes one predicate with its head, a modal or phasal verb (can leave, begins to leave); none by default auxiliary_form(token) method Verb form the checks of the clauses read for an auxiliary or a copula without VerbForm (predicate_form); by default an empty string, which skips it is_subordinate_clause_head(token) method Whether a clause head heads a subordinate clause, asked only of the words of is_clause_head; by default is_subordinate_clause_head of the module over the hooks is_clause_head and auxiliary_form is_infinitive_clause_head(token) method Whether a clause head heads an infinitive clause under a verb (wants to leave), counted apart from the subordinate ones; by default is_infinitive_clause_head of the module over the hooks is_clause_head and auxiliary_form is_prep_complement(token) method Whether a word is a link of a prepositional chain; by default is_prep_complement of the module with join_hyphens of the class is_participle_clause(token) method Whether a word heads a participial clause; by default a participle that is not the head of the sentence, has no auxiliary or copula and has a dependent (calc_valency) is_passive(token) method Whether a word is a passive verb form; by default is_passive of the module with join_hyphens of the class is_agentless(token) method Whether a passive form has no agent; by default the hook is_passive without an agent (has_agent of the module) is_negation(token) method Whether a word is a word of negation; by default Polarity=Neg or a word of negation_words, a conjunction excluded find_split_predicates(words) method Pairs of a light verb and the noun that carries its meaning (to make a decision); none by default negation_words class attribute Words of negation besides Polarity=Neg, in lower case; none by default join_hyphens class attribute Take a word the tokenizer split at its hyphens for one word, in the tree and in the default hooks requires_lemmas class attribute Whether the source must carry lemmas, for hooks that read them stats_desc, stats_headers class attributes Statistics of get_stats with their descriptions (SYNTAX_STATS_DESC by default), headers of the columns for print_stats messages class attribute Messages of the errors by key; MESSAGES by default

The subclass adds the statistics of the constructions of its language (chains of complements by calc_modifier_chains, its own clauses) in its constructor from sents, with its own stats_desc. A negation_words that is not a collection of strings raises SourceTypeError when the class is defined, and so does a parse that does not return a Doc when the statistics are computed.

docs.title: Shannon entropy
docs.text:
shannon_entropy(counts)

The Shannon entropy in bits of a distribution given by the count of every value, such as a Counter, with \(p_i\) the share of a value:

\[ -\sum_i p_i \log_2 p_i \]

One value gives 0, no counts or only zero ones nan; a zero count is left out, as \(0 \log_2 0 = 0\).

Parameter Type Default Description counts dict[object, int] - Count of every value

A negative, nan or infinite count raises SourceError.

check_sequence(value, what='words', ordered=True)

docs.title: Labels of a plot
docs.text:
merge_labels(defaults, labels, **samples)

Merges the labels given for a plot over its default ones; a label not given keeps its default. A default with fields in braces, such as "Moving average ({window})", is a format string: a label given for it may use only those fields, with a literal brace doubled ({{), and is tried on sample values of the fields, so that a format spec the values do not take ({window:s} for a number) fails before a figure is created. The other labels are taken as they are.

Parameter Type Default Description defaults dict[str, str] - Default labels by key labels dict[str, str] - Labels given; None - the default ones **samples object - Values of the fields of the format labels, for trying the labels given

Labels that are not a mapping of strings or have an unknown key raise ParameterError, and so does a label of a format default that is not a format string or has a field its default lacks or a format spec its values do not take.

The defaults of the visualizers of the core are anyts.constants.VISUALIZER_LABELS, by the name of the function.

from anyts.utils import merge_labels

merge_labels({"title": "Plot", "xlabel": "x"}, {"title": "My plot"})
merge_labels({"title": "Moving average ({window})"}, {"title": "Window of {size}"}, window=100)

docs.title: Lazy packages
docs.text: A package that imports its names on first use, so a light name does not load the dependencies of a heavy one.

docs.title: Lazy import
docs.text:
make_lazy(name, modules)

Turns a package into a LazyPackage: every name of the mapping modules is imported from its module of the package when it is first read. Importing the package then loads only what it imports itself, so the highlighting does not load matplotlib and a module of statistics does not load spaCy with the components. A module of the package is also its attribute on first use, and a module named as one of its functions (zipf) leaves the function under that name. A package calls it at the end of its __init__ with __name__; a TYPE_CHECKING block imports the same names for the type checkers.

Parameter Type Default Description name str - Name of the package, imported modules dict[str, str] - Module of the package by name

A name that is not a string or a mapping that is not one of strings to strings raises SourceTypeError; a name that is not that of an imported package, a lazy name that is not an identifier and a module that is not a dotted name of identifiers raise ParameterError.

# The __init__ of a package
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING

from anyts.utils import make_lazy

if TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .highlight import Highlight
    from .zipf import zipf

__all__ = ["Highlight", "zipf"]

make_lazy(__name__, {"Highlight": "highlight", "zipf": "zipf"})

docs.title: Class of a lazy package
docs.text:
LazyPackage is the class of a package after make_lazy, a subclass of types.ModuleType. It imports a name of its mapping on first read and keeps it as its attribute, gives a module of the package as an attribute, and lists the names of the mapping in dir(): those of __all__ if the package has it, so that help() and inspect.getmembers() import only the public names. A name that is neither raises AttributeError, a module that fails to import for a missing dependency raises its ModuleNotFoundError, and an AttributeError raised while a module imports comes as an ImportError with it as the cause, since Python would take it for a missing name.

docs.title: Doc, Span, Token and Language objects
docs.text:
is_doc(value)

Checks whether a value is a Doc object of spaCy without importing spaCy: such an object exists only once spaCy is loaded, so before that every value gives False. A library checks its sources this way to keep its import free of spaCy.

Parameter Type Default Description value object - Value to check 
is_span(value)

Checks whether a value is a Span object of spaCy, without importing spaCy as is_doc.

Parameter Type Default Description value object - Value to check 
is_token(value)

Checks whether a value is a Token object of spaCy, without importing spaCy as is_doc.

Parameter Type Default Description value object - Value to check 
is_language(value)

Checks whether a value is a Language pipeline of spaCy, without importing spaCy as is_doc: a library checks a pipeline passed to it this way.

Parameter Type Default Description value object - Value to check CodeResult 
import spacy

from anyts.utils import is_doc, is_language, is_span, is_token

nlp = spacy.blank("en")
doc = nlp("The cat sleeps")
is_doc(doc), is_doc(doc[:2]), is_span(doc[:2]), is_doc("The cat sleeps")
is_language(nlp), is_language("en_core_web_sm"), is_token(doc[0])

docs.title: Sentence boundaries
docs.text:
has_sents(doc)

Checks whether a Doc has its sentence boundaries: they count when every token has them, as after the parser, senter or sentencizer. The starts of a component that leaves the other tokens unset, such as start_sents_after_blank_lines without the parser, are partial; the statistics, kwic, sentence_lengths and the highlighting take the sentences of such a Doc from its text.

Parameter Type Default Description doc Doc - Doc object CodeResult 
import spacy

from anyts.components import start_sents_after_blank_lines
from anyts.utils import has_sents

nlp = spacy.blank("xx")
text = "Notes\n\nThe cat sleeps. The dog eats."
doc = start_sents_after_blank_lines(nlp(text))
doc.has_annotation("SENT_START"), has_sents(doc)
_ = nlp.add_pipe("sentencizer")
has_sents(nlp(text))

(True, False)
True

docs.text:
is_word(token)

Checks whether a token is a word: not whitespace and not a token of is_punctuation, so symbols like %, €, + and invisible characters are no words either. The words of iter_doc_tokens and the nodes of the dependency tree of the syntactic statistics are such tokens.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token CodeResult 
import spacy

from anyts.utils import is_word

doc = spacy.blank("en")("A 10% raise!")
[(token.text, is_word(token)) for token in doc]

[('A', True), ('10', True), ('%', False), ('raise', True), ('!', False)]

has_feature(token, field, value)

from spacy.tokens import Doc
from spacy.vocab import Vocab

from anyts.utils import has_feature

docs.text:
is_finite_verb(token)

Checks whether a token is a finite verb: the part of speech VERB with VerbForm=Fin, so a finite auxiliary (AUX) is not one.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token 
is_infinitive(token)

Checks whether a token is an infinitive, VerbForm=Inf whatever its part of speech.

from spacy.tokens import Doc

from anyts.utils import is_finite_verb, is_infinitive

doc = Doc(
    Vocab(),
    words=["She", "has", "to", "go"],

docs.title: Parts of hyphenated words
docs.text:
joins_previous(token)

Checks whether a token continues a word the tokenizer split at its hyphens (well-known into well, -, known): the token is a word right after a hyphen that follows a word, with no whitespace around the hyphen and no sentence starting at the hyphen or the token. iter_doc_units and the functions of the dependency tree join the parts of a word by this rule with join_hyphens=True.

Parameter Type Default Description token Token - Token CodeResult 
import spacy

from anyts.utils import joins_previous

doc = spacy.blank("en")("A well-known cat - and a dog")
[token.text for token in doc if joins_previous(token)]

['known']

docs.title: Tokens of the words
docs.text:
iter_doc_tokens(source)

Yields the tokens of the words of a Doc or a Span (is_word): whitespace tokens and the tokens of is_punctuation, symbols like % and € included, are skipped.

Parameter Type Default Description source Doc / Span - Doc or Span object CodeResult 
import spacy

from anyts.utils import iter_doc_tokens

doc = spacy.blank("xx")("A well-known cat!")
[token.text for token in iter_doc_tokens(doc)]

['A', 'well', 'known', 'cat']

docs.title: Words as lists of tokens
docs.text:
iter_doc_units(source, join_hyphens=False)

Yields the words of a Doc or a Span as lists of tokens: one token each, as in iter_doc_tokens. With join_hyphens=True a word that the tokenizer split at its hyphens (well-known into well, -, known) is joined back by the rule of joins_previous; a language library whose tokenizer keeps such words whole turns it on, so that a string and a Doc give the same words.

Parameter Type Default Description source Doc / Span - Doc or Span object join_hyphens bool False Join the parts of hyphenated words CodeResult 
from anyts.utils import iter_doc_units

[[token.text for token in unit] for unit in iter_doc_units(doc, join_hyphens=True)]

[['A'], ['well', '-', 'known'], ['cat']]

docs.text:
iter_doc_words(source, join_hyphens=False)

Yields the words of iter_doc_units as tuples: the position of the first character, the position after the last character and the text of the word. A byte order mark glued to the start of a word, as in a file read with utf-8 instead of utf-8-sig, is dropped.

Parameter Type Default Description source Doc / Span - Doc or Span object join_hyphens bool False Join the parts of hyphenated words CodeResult 
from anyts.utils import iter_doc_words

[word for _, _, word in iter_doc_words(doc)]
list(iter_doc_words(doc, join_hyphens=True))

['A', 'well', 'known', 'cat']
[(0, 1, 'A'), (2, 12, 'well-known'), (13, 16, 'cat')]

docs.title: Words by sentences
docs.text:
split_doc_units(source, sents_extractor, join_hyphens=False)

Splits the words of a Doc or a Span into the sentences of a sentence extractor, for a Doc without sentence boundaries or one to split otherwise: the sentences are found in its text in their order, and a word of iter_doc_units belongs to the sentence its first token lies in. The words outside the sentences found, those the extractor drops, are left out, so no sentence found gives no words.

Parameter Type Default Description source Doc / Span - Doc or Span object sents_extractor SentsExtractor - Sentence extraction tool join_hyphens bool False Join the parts of hyphenated words CodeResult 
import spacy

from anyts import SentsExtractor
from anyts.utils import split_doc_units

doc = spacy.blank("xx")("The cat sleeps. The dog eats.")
[[unit[0].text for unit in sent] for sent in split_doc_units(doc, SentsExtractor())]
[[unit[0].text for unit in sent] for sent in split_doc_units(doc, SentsExtractor(min_len=14))]

[['The', 'cat', 'sleeps'], ['The', 'dog', 'eats']]
[['The', 'cat', 'sleeps']]

docs.title: Marks between the words of a sentence
docs.text:
find_unit_marks(units)

Finds the punctuation marks between the words of a sentence of a Doc: the words are those of iter_doc_units, and a word with a character of is_punctuation between it and the word before gets its position, except a quote, an apostrophe and the hyphen that joins two parts of a word, as find_marks does for a text.

Parameter Type Default Description units list[list[Token]] - Tokens of every word of a sentence CodeResult 
import spacy

from anyts.utils import find_unit_marks, iter_doc_units

doc = spacy.blank("en")("So, it is late - very late")
sorted(find_unit_marks(list(iter_doc_units(doc))))

[1, 4]

docs.title: Tokenizer rules
docs.text:
add_tokenizer_rules(nlp, prefixes=(), suffixes=(), infixes=(), abbreviations=())

Adds the rules of a language to the tokenizer of a pipeline, so that the tokens of a Doc match the words a library splits a string into. The prefixes (such as the dashes of a dialogue glued to a word), suffixes and infixes are regular expressions joined to those of the tokenizer, every branch of a prefix anchored at the start and of a suffix at the end. An abbreviation becomes a single token in lower case, capitalized and in upper case when the tokenizer keeps one of its forms whole. A rule the tokenizer already has as a top-level alternative is not added twice; a tokenizer that is not the Tokenizer of spaCy, or whose rules are not regular expressions, is left as it is. A rule is joined to others, so it sets its flags in a group, (?i:...).

Parameter Type Default Description nlp Language - Pipeline whose tokenizer gets the rules prefixes list[str] () Patterns of the prefixes, without the anchor suffixes list[str] () Patterns of the suffixes, without the anchor infixes list[str] () Patterns of the infixes abbreviations list[str] / set[str] () Abbreviations in lower case

Rules that are not lists of strings and abbreviations that are not a collection of strings raise SourceTypeError, a rule that is not a regular expression that can be joined to others ParameterError.

CodeResult 
import spacy

from anyts.utils import add_tokenizer_rules

nlp = spacy.blank("en")
[token.text for token in nlp("--No, he said.")]
add_tokenizer_rules(nlp, prefixes=[r"-{2,}(?=\w)"])
[token.text for token in nlp("--No, he said.")]

['--No', ',', 'he', 'said', '.']
['--', 'No', ',', 'he', 'said', '.']

docs.title: Words and tokens
docs.text: Checks of the words of a text and the counts of their letters.

docs.title: Punctuation
docs.text:
is_punctuation(token)

Checks whether a token consists only of punctuation marks and symbols: the characters of the Unicode categories P (punctuation), S (symbols), M (combining marks) and Cf (invisible format characters such as the zero-width space U+200B, the byte order mark U+FEFF and the zero-width joiner U+200D). So ?!, --, €, №, a lone invisible character and an empty token are punctuation, and a token with a letter or a digit is not (e with a combining acute accent is a word). The results are cached by token, so the function is meant for tokens, not whole texts.

Parameter Type Default Description token str - Token CodeResult 
from anyts.utils import is_punctuation

is_punctuation("?!"), is_punctuation("€"), is_punctuation("no.")

(True, True, False)

docs.title: Numbers
docs.text:
is_number(word, pattern=NUMBER_PATTERN)

Checks whether a word is a number by a pattern matched against the whole lower-cased word; a language passes its own (ordinals, Roman numerals).

Parameter Type Default Description word str - Word pattern Pattern NUMBER_PATTERN Pattern of a number; by default the numbers of WordsExtractor CodeResult 
import re

from anyts.utils import is_number

is_number("2020"), is_number("10%"), is_number("3rd"), is_number("XIV", re.compile(r"[ivxlcdm]+"))

(True, True, False, True)

docs.text:
count_letters(word)

Counts the letters of a word: the characters of any alphabet (str.isalpha), without digits, hyphens and marks. The results are cached by word form, so the function is meant for words, not whole texts.

Parameter Type Default Description word str - Word form CodeResult

count_letters("well-known"), count_letters("3rd")

docs.text:
has_words(source)

Checks whether a text, a Doc or a Span holds a word: an empty text or one of whitespace and the characters of is_punctuation alone holds none.

docs.title: Marks between the words of a text
docs.text:
find_marks(text, words)

Finds the punctuation marks between the words of a text: the words are found in the text in their order, a word inside a longer one not counting, and a word with a character of is_punctuation between it and the word before gets its position; a quote, an apostrophe and the hyphen that joins two parts of a word are no marks. A word the text does not hold is passed over. The positions go to ConnectorMatcher.find, whose rules do not read a word across a mark.

Parameter Type Default Description text str - Text words list[str] - Words of the text in their order

A text that is not a string and words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Corpus plots
docs.text: Plots for the corpus measures: the lexical dispersion (where in a text a word occurs), a chart of the keywords of keyness and a network of the collocations of collocations. The matplotlib functions take the axes ax, a new figure without them, and return Axes; the network is a graphviz Graph, as the word tree is a Digraph.

docs.title: Lexical dispersion
docs.text:
dispersion_plot(words, targets, ax=None, labels=None)

A row for every word of targets and a tick at the position of each of its occurrences in the text. Words are compared as they are: case and lemmatization belong to the extraction of the words.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of the text in order targets list[str] - Words whose occurrences are shown ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel

Words or targets that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, no words or no targets SourceError; labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Chart of keywords
docs.text:
keyness_plot(positive, negative=(), top_n=20, labels=None, field='score', log=False, ax=None)

Diverging horizontal bars: the words of positive to the right, of negative (the result of keyness with positive=False) to the left, top_n on each side. The length of a bar is the absolute value of the field (score, g2, log_ratio), so the side is set by the list, not by the sign of the measure; words with an undefined or infinite value are skipped. For the odds ratio (from 0 to infinity, one - equal odds) log=True plots the absolute \(\log_2\) of the value, symmetric around one.

Parameter Type Default Description positive list[Keyword] - Positive keywords negative list[Keyword] () Negative keywords top_n int 20 Number of words on each side labels dict[str, str] / tuple[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel and xlabel_log (format strings with field), target and reference (the legend); a pair of strings sets the legend alone field str 'score' Field of Keyword whose values are plotted log bool False Plot \(\log_2\) of the value - for the odds ratio ax Axes None Axes for the plot

Keywords that are not a list raise SourceTypeError, and no keyword with a finite value SourceError. An unknown field, a top_n that is not an integer of at least one, labels that merge_labels refuses or a legend that is not a pair, and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Network of collocations
docs.text:
collocation_network(collocations, top_n=None)

An undirected graph in the neato layout: the nodes are the words, the size of the font by frequency, the edges the pairs, the width and the label by the measure. A pair of a word with itself (a word repeated within the window) would be a loop and is left out before top_n. Rendering needs the executables of Graphviz; Jupyter displays the graph, and graph.render("network") saves a png file.

Parameter Type Default Description collocations list[Collocation] - Collocations top_n int None Number of pairs from the start of the list; None - all of them

Collocations that are not a list raise SourceTypeError, no pair of two different words SourceError, and a top_n that is not an integer of at least one ParameterError.

from anyts.corpus import collocations, keyness
from anyts.visualizers import collocation_network, dispersion_plot, keyness_plot

target = "the cat sleeps and the cat eats and the cat purrs".split()
reference = "the dog sleeps and the dog eats and the dog barks".split()
dispersion_plot(target, ["cat", "eats"])
keyness_plot(keyness(target, reference), keyness(target, reference, positive=False))
print(collocation_network(collocations(target, window=1)).source)

docs.title: Literature fingerprinting
docs.text:
fingerprinting(texts, segment_len=10, metric=None, x_size=800, y_size=600, cmap='viridis', ax=None, labels=None)

Visualization of literature fingerprinting (Keim and Oelke 2007).

Every text is cut into segments of segment_len words with a sliding step of a tenth of a segment, and a measure of lexical diversity is computed for every segment. All segments are segment_len words long, so the values are comparable: when the step leaves words after the last segment, one more ends with the text, and a text not longer than a segment is one segment.

A text is a block of squares, its segments row by row, 8 rows high, or one column with at most 8 segments; a block wider than the drawing area wraps into rows of that width. The blocks go left to right and wrap within an area 2 · x_size wide, which grows downwards from 2 · y_size when they need more height. The colorbar runs from the smallest to the greatest finite value over all the texts; undefined values (nan on segments too short for the measure) and the empty cells of a block are light grey, unlike any value, zero included.

from anyts.diversity_stats import calc_mattr
from anyts.visualizers import fingerprinting

texts = [
    ("the cat sat on the mat " * 20).split(),
    " ".join(f"word{index % 37}" for index in range(150)).split(),
]
fingerprinting(texts, segment_len=20, metric=calc_mattr)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description texts list[list[str]] - List of lists of words segment_len int 10 Size of a segment metric Callable None Function of a measure of lexical diversity; calc_ttr by default x_size int 800 Half the width of the drawing area, greater than 25 (the margin between the blocks) y_size int 600 Half the height of the drawing area, which grows when the blocks need more cmap str 'viridis' Colour map ax Axes None Axes of matplotlib for the plot; if not given, a 15×10 figure is created labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title

The function returns the Axes with the visualization, set to an equal aspect so the squares stay square; the figure is ax.figure. Texts that are not a list of lists of strings and a metric that cannot be called raise SourceTypeError, a list without texts or a text without words SourceError. A segment_len or a y_size that is not an integer above zero, an x_size that is not an integer above 25, an unknown cmap, labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Text highlighting
docs.text:
HighlightedText(source, layers=None)

Highlighting of a text by layers, in the manner of the style checkers: every layer marks the fragments of a text that a statistic counts - long sentences, complex words, the passive. The data source is a text or a Doc object of spaCy. The result shows in Jupyter as HTML with styles and a legend; to_html returns the markup, and highlights keeps the fragments for a rendering of one's own. Fragments of different layers may overlap.

Raises:

  • SourceTypeError - a source that is neither a string nor a Doc;
  • SourceError - a source without words;
  • ParameterError - layers that are not a name or a list of names, a layer that is unknown or one that needs an annotation the source lacks.

A layer of the long sentences in a subclass.

CodeResult 
from anyts.visualizers import Highlight, HighlightedText


class Highlighter(HighlightedText):
    layers_desc = {"long_sents": "long sentence"}
    default_layers = ("long_sents",)
    layer_styles = {"long_sents": "background: #fef9c3;"}
    css_prefix = "demo"

    def find(self, layer, words, sents, doc):
        return [
            Highlight(sent.start, sent.end, layer, f"{sent.n_words} words")
            for sent in sents
            if sent.n_words >= 8
        ]


ht = Highlighter("The cat sleeps. The dog barks at the cat that sleeps on the mat.")
ht.highlights

(Highlight(start=16, end=64, layer='long_sents', note='11 words'),)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Type Default Description source str / Doc - Data source (a string or a Doc object) layers list[str] / str None Layers of the highlighting; if not given, the default layers the source allows; "all" - every layer allowed

docs.title: Attributes
docs.text:
Attribute Type Description text str Text of the data source layers tuple[str] Layers turned on, in the order of drawing highlights tuple[Highlight] Highlighted fragments, sorted by their start and then by descending end counts dict[str, int] Number of fragments of every layer 
Highlight(start, end, layer, note='')

A fragment of the highlighting: an immutable object with the parameters as its fields.

Field Type Default Description start int - Position of the first character of the fragment in the text end int - Position after the last character of the fragment layer str - Layer of the highlighting note str '' Explanation of the fragment for the tooltip

docs.title: Methods
docs.text:
to_html(legend=True, css=True) returns the HTML markup of the highlighted text: a div of the class <prefix>-highlight with the legend, its counts and the text, where a highlighted segment is a span of the classes <prefix>-hl and <prefix>-hl-<layer> with the notes in its title; <prefix> is css_prefix. Overlapping fragments of different layers give segments with several classes, in the order of drawing. Line breaks (\n, \r\n, \r) become character references, one per break, so the markup can go into Markdown.

Parameter Type Default Description legend bool True Add the legend with the counts of the fragments css bool True Add the styles of the layers

The class method css() returns the styles to_html adds: the container, the legend and the text under the classes of css_prefix, the declarations of layer_styles for every layer, and a dark colour of the text on the layers with a background.

CodeResult 
ht.to_html(legend=False, css=False)

'<div class="demo-highlight"><div class="demo-highlight-text">The cat sleeps. <span class="demo-hl demo-hl-long_sents" title="11 words">The dog barks at the cat that sleeps on the mat.</span></div></div>'

docs.title: Helpers of the layers
docs.text:
The helpers and the finders of the layers are in anyts.visualizers.highlight.

Word(start, end, text, pos=None, lemma=None)

A word with its position in the text and, when known, its part of speech and lemma.

Sent(start, end, n_words)

A sentence with its position and number of words.

get_doc_words(doc)

The words of iter_doc_tokens with their positions, a byte order mark at the start of the text left out, with the part of speech and the lemma when the Doc has them.

iter_doc_sents(doc)

The sentences of the boundaries of a Doc as triples of the start, the end and the text; the whitespace tokens at the edges of a sentence are left out, and a sentence of whitespace alone is skipped.

get_text_sents(spans, words)

The sentences given by their positions with their numbers of words; a word belongs to the sentence of its first character.

group_words_by_sents(words, sents)

The words of every sentence; the words out of the sentences are skipped.

tokens_span(tokens)

The positions of the fragment that covers some tokens, without the punctuation and the whitespace at its edges.

split_segments(length, highlights)

The segments of a text with the same set of fragments: their bounds are the starts and the ends of all the fragments, and overlapping or nested fragments give segments with several layers.

docs.title: Finders of the layers
docs.text: The layers the languages share are found by functions that take the language as parameters: the notes of the fragments (callables where they read a number, so a language writes its plural forms; English by default), the counts of syllables, the normalized forms of the words, the stems, the matcher of the connectors. A subclass calls them from its find. A value that cannot be called for a parameter that takes a function, such as count_syllables, normalize or stem, raises SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Long sentences
docs.text:
find_long_sents(sents, long_sent_word_factor, note=None)

The layer long_sents: the sentences of long_sent_word_factor words or more.

Parameter Type Default Description sents list[Sent] - Sentences with their positions and numbers of words long_sent_word_factor int - Minimum number of words of a long sentence note Callable[[int], str] None Note of a sentence by its number of words

A long_sent_word_factor that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Complex words
docs.text:
find_complex_words(words, complex_syl_factor, count_syllables, note=None)

The layer complex_words: the words of complex_syl_factor syllables of count_syllables or more.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[Word] - Words with their positions complex_syl_factor int - Minimum number of syllables of a complex word count_syllables Callable[[str], int] - Number of the syllables of a word note Callable[[int], str] None Note of a word by its number of syllables

A complex_syl_factor that is not an integer of at least one raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Single words
docs.text:
find_words(words, is_match, layer, note='')

A layer of single words, such as stopwords, rare words or verbal nouns: the words the check is_match of a language accepts.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[Word] - Words with their positions, parts of speech and lemmas is_match Callable[[Word], bool] - Whether a word is a fragment of the layer layer str - Layer of the highlighting note str '' Note of every fragment

docs.title: Phrases
docs.text:
find_phrase_highlights(words, phrases, layer, note=None, normalize=str.lower)

A layer of the phrases of a list, such as compound prepositions, clichés or parentheticals. The phrases are matched by the normalized forms of their words, each normalized alone as in the text (find_phrases). A mapping gives their variants - contractions, forms of verbs - with the phrase each stands for; of the variants that normalize alike the first wins. A set of phrases is read in order (in_order). A fragment spans the phrase in the text; its note reads the phrase of the list, in quotes by default.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[Word] - Words with their positions phrases list[str] / dict[str, str] - Phrases, words separated by spaces, or their variants with the phrase of each layer str - Layer of the highlighting note Callable[[str], str] None Note of a fragment by its phrase normalize Callable[[str], str] str.lower Normalized form of a word

Phrases that are not a collection of strings or a mapping of strings raise SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Connectors
docs.text:
find_connector_highlights(words, sents, matcher, note=None, pos=None, text=None, blocked=None)

The layer connectors: the connectors of a ConnectorMatcher of the language inside every sentence, in the whole text when the sentences are None; a one-word connector is checked by its part of speech when a word of the sentence has one - its own, or that of the hook pos. With the text, a character of is_punctuation between two words is a punctuation mark, which the rules of the matcher do not read through; a quote, an apostrophe and the hyphen that joins two parts of a word are none. No connector starts at a word the hook blocked rules out, such as one its parse makes no connector. The note gives the text, the class and the kind of the connector by default.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[Word] - Words with their positions and parts of speech sents list[Sent] - Sentences with their positions matcher ConnectorMatcher - Matcher of the connectors of a language note Callable[[Connector], str] None Note of a connector pos Callable[[Word], str] None Part of speech of a word for the matcher text str None Text of the words, for the punctuation marks between them blocked Callable[[Word], bool] None Whether no connector starts at a word

A hook that cannot be called or a text that is not a string raises SourceTypeError.

docs.title: Split predicates
docs.text:
find_split_predicate_highlights(pairs, note=None)

The layer split_predicates: a fragment for every pair of a light verb and its noun a language finds, from the first word of the pair to the last; the note reads their lemmas by default.

Parameter Type Default Description pairs list[tuple[Token, Token]] - Light verb and noun of every split predicate note Callable[[Token, Token], str] None Note of a pair

docs.title: Runs of alliteration
docs.text:
calc_alliteration_runs(words, frequencies, threshold=0.001, stem=list, is_transparent=None)

The runs of two or more neighbouring words with a consonant of frequencies in the stem of each (the stem of a language leaves out the endings that repeat by agreement) and a probability below the threshold. The probability under an independent spread of the consonants is the product over the words of \(1 - (1 - f)^n\), \(f\) the frequency of the consonant and \(n\) the length of the stem. A transparent word - by default one shorter than ALLITERATION_MIN_WORD_LEN (3) letters, a stopword for a language - neither breaks nor continues a run; the words are taken in lower case. A run is a triple of the index of its first word, the index after its last word and its consonant, in the order of the text.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of a sentence frequencies dict[str, float] - Consonants to look for with their frequencies threshold float 0.001 Probability threshold (anyts.constants.ALLITERATION_THRESHOLD) stem Callable[[str], list[str]] list Sounds or letters of the stem of a word; the letters of the word by default is_transparent Callable[[str], bool] None Whether a word neither breaks nor continues a run

Words that are not a list of strings and frequencies that are not a mapping of strings to numbers raise SourceTypeError, and a frequency outside [0, 1] or a threshold outside (0, 1] ParameterError.

docs.title: Alliteration
docs.text:
find_alliteration(words, sents, frequencies, threshold=0.001, stem=list, is_transparent=None, note=None)

The layer alliteration: the runs of calc_alliteration_runs inside every sentence, in the whole text when the sentences are None.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[Word] - Words with their positions sents list[Sent] - Sentences with their positions note Callable[[str], str] None Note of a run by its consonant

The other arguments are those of calc_alliteration_runs; the frequencies and the threshold raise its errors.

docs.title: For library developers
docs.text:
Language hooks of a subclass

The core has no layers of its own: a language library subclasses HighlightedText and sets its layers and their search.

Hook Kind Description layers_desc class attribute The layers in the order of drawing with their names in the legend, dict[str, str] default_layers class attribute The layers on by default, among those the source allows, tuple[str] layer_annotations class attribute The annotations of a Doc a layer needs (DEP, POS, LEMMA...), dict[str, tuple[str]]; a layer without them is available for a string too layer_styles class attribute The CSS declarations of every layer, dict[str, str]; the text of a layer with a background keeps a dark colour on it css_prefix class attribute The prefix of the CSS classes, str find(layer, words, sents, doc) method The fragments of a layer: a list of Highlight from the words and the sentences of the text and the Doc (None for a string) iter_words(text), iter_sents(text) methods The words and the sentences of a string as triples of the start, the end and the text; by default those of the default tokenizers of WordsExtractor and SentsExtractor doc_words(doc) method The words of a Doc; by default get_doc_words annotation_names class attribute Names of the annotations in the message of a layer a source does not allow, dict[str, str]; English by default messages class attribute Messages of the errors by key; MESSAGES by default

The sentences of a Doc come from its boundaries, or from iter_sents over its text when it has none or partial ones (has_sents). iter_sents gets the parts of a text between blank lines one by one, so a blank line always ends a sentence; a sentence holds the words of doc_words or iter_words that start in it. find runs in __init__: a subclass stores its own parameters, checked by check_params, before calling the __init__ of the base, and may find its layers with the finders of the layers. A fragment of another layer, an empty one or one outside the text raises ParameterError; a find that does not return Highlight objects, and an iter_words or an iter_sents whose triples are not ascending integer bounds inside the text with the text of each, SourceTypeError.

In the core the layers are empty and css_prefix is anyts.

check_params(long_sent_word_factor, complex_syl_factor, alliteration_threshold, *, messages=MESSAGES)

Checks the parameters of the highlighting: a number of words or syllables that is not an integer of at least one, or a threshold outside the interval (0, 1], raises ParameterError.

docs.title: Sentence lengths
docs.text:
sentence_lengths_plot(source, window=10, inset=True, ax=None, labels=None, sents_extractor=None, words_extractor=None, join_hyphens=False)

The curve of the lengths of the sentences - the rhythm of a text: the length of every sentence in words, in order, the moving average over window sentences and an inset with the histogram of the lengths. Short and long sentences in turn are an editorial sign of a lively text, a flat curve of a monotonous one. The function takes the axes ax and returns Axes.

from anyts.visualizers import sentence_lengths_plot

text = "The cat sleeps. Does the dog? It eats, she said. Then both of them went out."
sentence_lengths_plot(text, window=2)

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description source str / Doc / Iterable[int] - Text, Doc object or lengths of the sentences (a list, a numpy array, a Series) window int 10 Window of the moving average in sentences inset bool True Show the inset with the histogram ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel, ylabel, length (the curve), average (a format string with window), distribution (the inset) sents_extractor SentsExtractor None Extractor of the sentences of a string; the sentence extractor of the library by default words_extractor WordsExtractor None Extractor of the words of a sentence of a string; the word extractor of the library by default

The source and the extractors raise the errors of sentence_lengths, and no sentences raise SourceError; a window that is not an integer of at least one, labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

The core functions also take join_hyphens, False by default, which joins the parts of hyphenated words of a Doc with sentence boundaries (iter_doc_words). The extractors of the core are SentsExtractor() and WordsExtractor().

docs.title: Lengths of the sentences
docs.text:
sentence_lengths(source, sents_extractor=None, words_extractor=None, join_hyphens=False)

The lengths of the sentences in words, in order: a string is split by the sentence and the word extractors, a Doc by its boundaries and iter_doc_words with join_hyphens, and a Doc without boundaries or with partial ones (has_sents) is counted as its text. Sentences without words are skipped. Ready lengths (non-negative integers in a sequence or an iterator) are used as they are. The arguments are those of sentence_lengths_plot.

A table, a set, a mapping, bytes, a length that is not an integer and an extractor of another type raise SourceTypeError, a negative length SourceError.

from anyts.visualizers import sentence_lengths

sentence_lengths("The cat sleeps. Does the dog? It eats, she said. Then both of them went out.")

[3, 3, 4, 6]

docs.title: Stylometric plots
docs.text: Plots for stylometry: a dendrogram and the multidimensional scaling of the matrix of distances of delta, the principal components of the frequencies of the most frequent words and the Mendenhall curves of several texts. The functions take the axes ax and return Axes.

docs.title: Dendrogram
docs.text:
dendrogram_plot(distances, method='ward', ax=None, labels=None)

Hierarchical clustering by scipy.cluster.hierarchy over the matrix of distances between texts, Ward's method by default as in Evert et al. (2015); the leaves are labelled by the index of the matrix. The columns are taken in the order of the rows.

Parameter Type Default Description distances DataFrame - Symmetric matrix of distances with the names of the texts in the rows and the columns, in any order method str 'ward' Method of scipy.cluster.hierarchy.linkage to join the clusters: single, complete, average, weighted, centroid, median or ward ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel

Other texts in the columns than in the rows, fewer than two texts, an infinite or negative distance, asymmetry or a distance on the diagonal raise SourceError before a figure is created. Distances that are not a DataFrame of numbers raise SourceTypeError; an unknown method, labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Principal components
docs.text:
pca_plot(corpus, n_mfw=100, culling=0.0, ax=None, labels=None)

Principal component analysis of the z-scores of the relative frequencies of the most frequent units (frequency_table, z_scores): the texts on the plane of the first two components with their names, the shares of the explained variance in the labels of the axes.

Parameter Type Default Description corpus dict[str, list[str]] - Units of the texts by the names of the texts n_mfw int 100 Number of the most frequent units; None - all of them culling float 0.0 Smallest share of the texts a unit occurs in ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel and ylabel (format strings with the explained share)

The corpus, n_mfw and culling raise the errors of frequency_table, and fewer than three texts raise SourceError; labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Multidimensional scaling
docs.text:
mds_plot(distances, ax=None, labels=None)

Classical multidimensional scaling (Torgerson 1952) of any matrix of distances: the two leading eigenvectors of the double-centred squared distances, so the distances between the points approximate those of the matrix. The columns are taken in the order of the rows.

Parameter Type Default Description distances DataFrame - Symmetric matrix of distances with the names of the texts in the rows and the columns, in any order ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel, ylabel

Other texts in the columns than in the rows, fewer than two texts, an infinite or negative distance, asymmetry or a distance on the diagonal raise SourceError before a figure is created. Distances that are not a DataFrame of numbers raise SourceTypeError; labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Mendenhall curves
docs.text:
mendenhall_plot(corpus, ax=None, labels=None)

The shares of the words by length in characters (mendenhall_curve) of every text on one plot; a length no word has is drawn at zero.

Parameter Type Default Description corpus dict[str, list[str]] - Words of the texts by the names of the texts ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel, ylabel

A corpus that is not a mapping of lists of strings raises SourceTypeError, no texts or a text without words SourceError; labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from anyts.corpus import delta
from anyts.visualizers import dendrogram_plot, mds_plot, mendenhall_plot, pca_plot

corpus = {
    "A": "the cat sat on the mat and the cat slept".split(),
    "B": "a dog lay on a rug and a dog barked".split(),
    "C": "the cat and a dog sat on the rug".split(),
}
distances = delta(corpus, n_mfw=5)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=(12, 10))
dendrogram_plot(distances, ax=axes[0, 0])
mds_plot(distances, ax=axes[0, 1])
pca_plot(corpus, n_mfw=5, ax=axes[1, 0])
mendenhall_plot(corpus, ax=axes[1, 1])

docs.title: Vocabulary growth and frequency spectrum
docs.text: Two plots of the distribution of the words of a text that complement Zipf's law: the growth of the vocabulary with the length of the text by Heaps' law and the frequency spectrum - how many word types occur exactly once, twice, three times. The functions take the axes ax and return Axes.

docs.title: Heaps' law
docs.text:
heaps_plot(words, ax=None, labels=None)

The size of the vocabulary \(V\) after every word of the text and the fitted curve \(V(N) = K \cdot N^{\beta}\) of fit_heaps with its parameters in the legend; the curve depends on the order of the words.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of the text in order ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel, ylabel, growth (the curve), fit (a format string with k and beta)

Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, fewer than two words SourceError; labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

docs.title: Frequency spectrum
docs.text:
frequency_spectrum_plot(words, ax=None, labels=None)

The number of word types \(V(m)\) that occur exactly \(m\) times (calc_frequency_spectrum) in logarithmic coordinates; the left edge is the hapaxes. The spectrum underlies the measures of diversity of Yule, Sichel, Michéa and Honoré, and its shape shows how far the vocabulary of the text is from being exhausted.

Parameter Type Default Description words list[str] - Words of the text ax Axes None Axes for the plot labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: title, xlabel, ylabel

Words that are not a list of strings raise SourceTypeError, no words SourceError; labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

from anyts import WordsExtractor
from anyts.visualizers import frequency_spectrum_plot, heaps_plot

text = "The cat sat on the mat and the dog sat on the rug, and the cat saw the dog."
words = WordsExtractor(lowercase=True).extract(text)
fig, (left, right) = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 4.5))
heaps_plot(words, ax=left)
frequency_spectrum_plot(words, ax=right)

wordtree(texts, keyword, max_n=5, max_per_n=8, **kwargs)

Building a word tree of the contexts of a keyword: the N-grams of up to max_n words that start or end with the keyword are counted in every list of words, such as a sentence. Every level keeps the max_per_n most frequent N-grams that continue a kept shorter one, alphabetically when equal; they are joined into two trees, after the keyword and before it, the size of the font by frequency (Wattenberg and Viégas 2008). Rendering needs the executables of Graphviz.

from anyts.visualizers import wordtree

sentences = [
    ["the", "cat", "sleeps"],
    ["the", "cat", "eats", "fish"],
    ["a", "black", "cat", "sleeps"],
]
tree = wordtree(sentences, "cat", max_n=3)
tree.render("wordtree")

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description texts list[list[str]] - List of lists of words keyword str - Keyword whose contexts are shown max_n int 5 Largest size of the context max_per_n int 8 Largest number of examples for every size of the context **kwargs - - Drawing parameters: max_font_size (default 30), min_font_size (12), font_interp - a function of the relative frequency of a node (its frequency over the greatest one, in (0, 1]) giving the share of the range from min_font_size to max_font_size, from 0 to 1; the cube root by default

The function returns a Digraph of graphviz. Texts that are not a list of lists of strings and a keyword that is not a string raise SourceTypeError; no texts, or a keyword with no word next to it in any of them, SourceError; a max_n that is not an integer of at least 2 and a max_per_n that is not an integer of at least one ParameterError.

docs.title: Zipf's law
docs.text:
zipf(counter, num_words=None, num_labels=10, log=True, show_theory=False, alpha=1.5, show_fit=False, ax=None, labels=None)

Plotting Zipf's law from a counter of the frequencies of words.

Definition

Zipf's law (the rank-frequency law) is an empirical regularity of the frequencies of words in a natural language: with the words of a language, or of a long enough text, ordered by descending frequency, the frequency of the n-th word is roughly inversely proportional to its rank n. The second most frequent word occurs about half as often as the first, the third a third as often, and so on.

from collections import Counter

from anyts import WordsExtractor
from anyts.visualizers import zipf

text = "The cat sat on the mat and the dog sat on the rug, and the cat saw the dog."
counts = Counter(WordsExtractor(lowercase=True).extract(text))
ax = zipf(counts, num_labels=5, show_fit=True, labels={"title": "Zipf's law of a sentence"})
ax.figure.savefig("zipf.png")

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Type Default Description counter Counter - Counter of the frequencies of words num_words int None Number of the most frequent words num_labels int 10 Number of the words labelled on the plot log bool True Use a logarithmic scale show_theory bool False Plot the theoretical Zipf's law alpha float 1.5 Exponent α of the theoretical Zipf's law, greater than zero show_fit bool False Plot the Zipf-Mandelbrot fit \(f(r) = C / (r + q)^s\) of fit_zipf_mandelbrot ax Axes None Axes of matplotlib for the plot; if not given, a new figure is created labels dict[str, str] None Labels of the plot over the defaults: title, xlabel, ylabel, experimental and theoretical (the curves), fit (a format string with q and s)

The function returns the Axes with the plot; a num_words greater than the number of word types does not extend the curves beyond the data. A counter that is not a Counter of strings raises SourceTypeError, and an empty counter or a frequency that is not above zero SourceError. A num_words below one, a negative num_labels, with show_theory an exponent that is not a finite number above zero, labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError. All of them are raised before a figure is created.

docs.text:
zipf_theory(size, num_ranks, alpha=1.5, ax=None, labels=None)

The theoretical curve alone, \(f(r) = size \cdot r^{-\alpha}\) for the ranks from 1 to num_ranks.

Parameter Type Default Description size int / float - Frequency of the first rank num_ranks int - Number of ranks alpha float 1.5 Exponent α ax Axes None Axes of matplotlib for the plot; if not given, a new figure is created labels dict[str, str] None Labels over the defaults: theoretical (the curve)

A size or an alpha that is not a finite number above zero, a num_ranks that is not an integer of at least one, labels that merge_labels refuses and an ax that is not a matplotlib Axes raise ParameterError.
